policies.name: Code of Business Conduct & Ethics
policies.owner: Ethics & Compliance (Chief Compliance Officer); HR Employee Relations for people-related sections
policies.approver: Board of Directors on recommendation of the Nominating & Governance (or Audit) Committee; General Counsel + CHRO for non-substantive updates
policies.review: Annual review; Board re-approval of material amendments; update on law change
policies.audience: All directors, officers, employees, interns and temporary staff worldwide; contractors, agency workers and business partners through contract flow-down
policies.purpose: Sets the Company's core standards of integrity and serves as the code of conduct required by Nasdaq Rule 5610 and the SOX Section 406 code of ethics for a US-listed issuer. It gives employees in every country one reference for expected conduct, how to raise concerns and how violations are handled, and anchors the enforceability of the policies that sit beneath it.
keyProvisions: The Code applies to every director, officer and employee of [Company] and its subsidiaries; contractors, agency workers and business partners are bound through contract terms and the Supplier Code.

The Code is publicly available on the investor relations website, published in English, Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese (and any language spoken by 10%+ of a site's workforce), and the English text prevails except where local law requires the local version to prevail.

Any waiver of the Code for a director or executive officer may be granted only by the Board (or a designated Board committee) and must be disclosed within four business days on Form 8-K Item 5.05 or on the website where Item 5.05(c) conditions are met; waivers for other employees require written approval of the Chief Compliance Officer and General Counsel and are logged.
Amendments to Code provisions covering the CEO, CFO, principal accounting officer or controller are disclosed within four business days in the same manner as waivers.

Every employee completes Code training within 30 days of hire and certifies annually that they have read and complied with the Code and disclosed conflicts; directors and officers certify through the annual D&O questionnaire.

The Code covers, at minimum: conflicts of interest and corporate opportunities, confidentiality and trade secrets, protection of assets, fair dealing, anti-bribery, export control and sanctions, insider trading, antitrust (including no-poach and wage-fixing agreements), accurate books and records, full and fair public disclosure, and a respectful, safe workplace.

Employees must report suspected violations promptly through a manager, HR, Legal, Ethics & Compliance or the Speak Up hotline (anonymous where lawful); retaliation against anyone who reports in good faith is prohibited.

Nothing in the Code or any Company agreement prevents anyone from reporting possible violations of law to, or communicating with, the SEC, DOJ, EEOC, NLRB, OSHA or any other government agency, participating in an investigation, or receiving a government award, and no notice to the Company is required (Rule 21F-17).
Nothing in the Code restricts US non-supervisory employees from discussing wages, hours or working conditions or engaging in other concerted activity protected by NLRA Section 7.
Managers must model the Code, escalate any concern they receive to HR or Ethics & Compliance within one business day and never discourage reporting; failure to escalate is itself a violation.
Violations lead to corrective action up to termination, applied consistently across countries and following local procedure (China handbook adoption, India domestic enquiry, Taiwan filed work rules).
Ethics & Compliance reports Code metrics (cases by category and country, substantiation rate, time to close, discipline outcomes, waivers) to the Audit Committee at least quarterly.
policies.sampleLanguage:
Our Commitment. [Company] designs the chips that power our customers' products, and our reputation for integrity is as important as our technology. This Code of Business Conduct and Ethics applies to every director, officer and employee of [Company] and its subsidiaries worldwide. You must follow this Code, all Company policies and the laws of every country where we do business. Where local law sets a stricter standard, follow the stricter standard.

Raising Concerns. If you see or suspect conduct that violates this Code, the law or Company policy, speak up. You may contact your manager, HR, Legal, Ethics & Compliance or the Speak Up hotline at [URL/number], which accepts anonymous reports where local law permits. [Company] will not tolerate retaliation against anyone who raises a concern in good faith or cooperates in an investigation.

Protected Rights. Nothing in this Code prohibits you from reporting possible violations of law to any government agency, communicating with the SEC or other regulators, or receiving an award for information provided, and you do not need to notify [Company] before doing so.

Waivers. Only the Board may waive this Code for a director or executive officer, and any such waiver will be publicly disclosed as required by law and Nasdaq rules.

roles.duties: Approves the Code and material amendments, and grants any waiver for directors or executive officers, which Legal then discloses within four business days.
Owns the Code, training and annual certification; runs the Speak Up program and reports Code metrics and waivers to the Audit Committee quarterly.
Localizes the Code into country handbooks and work rules, investigates people-related allegations and applies consistent corrective action.
Determines whether an exception is a reportable waiver and files 8-K Item 5.05 disclosures of waivers and amendments.
Model expected conduct, escalate every concern within one business day and protect reporters from retaliation.
Complete training within 30 days of hire, certify annually and raise concerns through any channel.

countryAddenda.us: Add an NLRA Section 7 savings clause (Stericycle remains binding despite the NLRB's new Republican majority) and the Rule 21F-17 protected-rights language, and carve SOX whistleblower claims out of any arbitration program. Make sure confidentiality and civility expectations do not restrict discussion of pay or working conditions, and cross-reference state lawful off-duty conduct protections (e.g., NY Labor Law 201-d).
countryAddenda.us-ca: Add the Gov Code 12964.5 carve-out (nothing prevents disclosing information about unlawful acts in the workplace such as harassment or discrimination) and note Labor Code 96(k)/98.6 protection of lawful off-duty conduct and 1101-1102 protection of political activity. Post the Labor Commissioner whistleblower notice (LC 1102.8) and apply a Legal review before disciplining anyone within 90 days of protected activity (SB 497 presumption).
countryAddenda.ca: Present the Code as a policy the employee agrees to follow, issued with the offer (or supported by new consideration) so discipline under it is enforceable; state that discipline follows just-cause principles and proportionality (McKinley v. BC Tel). Cross-reference the Ontario OHSA and BC WorkSafeBC harassment programs and Criminal Code s.425.1 protection for reporting offences to authorities, and provide a French version if any Quebec-based employee is covered.
countryAddenda.in: Incorporate the Code by reference into appointment letters and service rules or standing orders (mandatory at 300+ workers) so misconduct categories support a domestic enquiry. A Companies Act s.177 vigil mechanism is mandatory only if the Indian entity is listed or has public deposits or borrowings above INR 50 crore; otherwise the global hotline serves this purpose.
countryAddenda.tw: At 30+ employees, the Code's disciplinary content must be incorporated into work rules filed with the local labor authority (Science Park Bureau for Hsinchu Science Park sites) and posted (LSA Art. 70); issue a Traditional Chinese version, which prevails locally. Only misconduct listed in approved work rules supports discipline, and LSA Art. 12 dismissals must occur within 30 days of learning of the cause.
countryAddenda.cn: The Code cannot support discipline until adopted through democratic procedure (discussion with the employee congress or all employees and consultation with the union or employee representatives) and publicized with signed acknowledgment (LCL Art. 4); issue a Chinese version that prevails. Define 'serious violations' concretely so LCL Art. 39 dismissals are defensible, and handle hotline data under a PIPL notice with separate consent for cross-border transfer.

decisions: One global Code vs. Code plus country handbooks? (A single Code simplifies Nasdaq disclosure, but China and Taiwan require locally adopted or filed rules for discipline; most issuers keep a global Code that local handbooks incorporate.)

Who may grant waivers below executive level: CCO alone or CCO + General Counsel? (Dual approval with a waiver log is common; repeated 'exceptions' for executives can become undisclosed de facto waivers.)
Annual certification: standalone LMS attestation vs. bundled with the conflict-of-interest questionnaire? (Bundling lifts completion; separate attestations give cleaner evidence per employee.)
Publication languages: English plus Simplified and Traditional Chinese only, or also Hindi/Kannada? (Engineers usually work in English, but displayed notices in India need local language.)
Include a misconduct and discipline matrix in the Code or only principles? (A matrix aids enforceability in China, India and Taiwan but reduces US flexibility.)
Board committee owner: Audit Committee vs. Nominating & Governance? (Audit if the hotline and accounting complaints sit together; N&G if the Code is treated as governance.)
pitfalls: Approving executive exceptions informally (a related-party vendor, an outside board seat) without recognizing them as Code waivers that need Board approval and 8-K disclosure within four business days.
Confidentiality or 'contact Legal before any regulator' language that violates Rule 21F-17; the SEC fined Foot Locker $148,000 in May 2026 for award-waiver clauses.
Relying on a US-drafted Code to dismiss employees in China or Taiwan when it was never adopted by democratic procedure or incorporated into filed work rules.
Letting certification completion slip below 100% for officers, finance and sales staff, weakening the Code's evidentiary value in investigations and SOX walkthroughs.
Civility or non-disparagement language that restricts NLRA Section 7 activity.
policies.training: Code training within 30 days of hire; annual refresher and certification for all employees; directors and officers certify via the annual D&O questionnaire; re-acknowledgment on every material amendment.

policies.name: Speak Up & Non-Retaliation
policies.owner: Ethics & Compliance (hotline and case management); Employee Relations for people-related investigations
policies.approver: Audit Committee of the Board (SOX Section 301 complaint procedures); General Counsel + CHRO for procedural updates
policies.review: Annual; also after any retaliation finding or change in whistleblower law
policies.audience: All employees, officers and directors; former employees, contractors, agency workers, suppliers and other third parties may also use the channels
policies.purpose: Establishes multiple safe channels, including an anonymous hotline, for raising concerns about misconduct, sets how reports are triaged, investigated and escalated, and prohibits retaliation. It satisfies the Audit Committee's SOX Section 301 complaint-procedure requirement, supports defenses under SOX 806, Dodd-Frank and California Labor Code 1102.5, and protects the Company's ability to self-report to DOJ within the 120-day window.
keyProvisions: Concerns may be raised with any manager, HR, Legal, Ethics & Compliance, the Audit Committee chair (for accounting, internal controls and auditing matters) or the Speak Up hotline (web and phone, 24/7, in English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Hindi and Kannada), anonymously where local law permits.

Ethics & Compliance acknowledges each report within 2 business days, completes triage within 5 business days and assigns an independent investigator; no one may investigate a matter in which they are implicated or which concerns their own reporting line.

Complaints about accounting, internal accounting controls, auditing or securities fraud are logged for the Audit Committee; any matter involving an executive officer or potentially material financial impact is escalated to the Audit Committee chair within 48 hours.

Potential export-control, sanctions, FCPA, trade-secret or antitrust matters are escalated to the General Counsel within 24 hours so the Company can evaluate voluntary self-disclosure within the 120-day window of the DOJ Corporate Whistleblower Awards Pilot Program.

Retaliation (termination, demotion, pay or bonus reduction, adverse rating, exclusion from projects, threats, harassment, blacklisting) against anyone who reports in good faith, participates in an investigation or refuses to act unlawfully is prohibited and is itself grounds for termination.

Before any adverse action (termination, PIP, rating downgrade, RIF selection, equity forfeiture decision) affecting an employee who raised a concern in the prior 12 months, Employee Relations completes a protected-activity check and Legal approves the action.
Reporter and witness identities are shared only on a need-to-know basis, and the Company will not attempt to identify anonymous reporters.

Nothing in this policy or any agreement prevents reporting to, or communicating with, the SEC, DOJ, OSHA, EEOC, NLRB or any other government agency, or receiving a government award, without notice to the Company; separation agreements may waive only recovery from the Company.
Reporters are told when their matter is closed and, where appropriate, the general outcome, subject to privacy and privilege.
Ethics & Compliance monitors each identified reporter's employment outcomes for 24 months after closure to detect retaliation.
Case metrics (volume by category and country, substantiation rate, median days to close, retaliation allegations) are reported to the Audit Committee quarterly.
Hotline and investigation records are retained for 7 years after closure unless a legal hold or local law requires a different period.
policies.sampleLanguage:
How to Speak Up. If you believe that someone acting on behalf of [Company] has violated the law, our Code of Business Conduct or any Company policy, we want to know. You may raise a concern with your manager, any member of HR, Legal or Ethics & Compliance, or through the Speak Up hotline at [URL] or [local numbers], which is operated by an independent provider and available 24 hours a day in multiple languages. Where local law permits, you may report anonymously. Concerns about accounting, internal controls or auditing matters may also be sent directly to the Chair of the Audit Committee at [address].

What Happens Next. Ethics & Compliance will acknowledge your report within two business days and assign an impartial reviewer. We will keep your identity confidential to the fullest extent possible and tell you when the matter is closed.

No Retaliation. [Company] prohibits retaliation against anyone who raises a concern in good faith, participates in an investigation or refuses to act unlawfully. Anyone who retaliates will face discipline up to and including termination.

Your Rights. Nothing in this policy limits your right to report possible violations of law to, or communicate with, any government agency, or to receive an award for information provided, without notice to [Company].

roles.duties: Approves the SOX 301 complaint procedures, receives quarterly case reports and oversees matters involving executive officers or financial reporting.
Operates the hotline, triages within 5 business days, assigns investigators, runs retaliation monitoring and reports metrics.
Investigates people-related concerns and performs protected-activity checks before adverse actions.
Directs privileged investigations, decides on self-disclosure within the 120-day window, audits templates for Rule 21F-17 and issues legal holds.
Receive concerns respectfully, escalate within one business day without investigating on their own and avoid any retaliatory action.
Report concerns promptly and in good faith and cooperate truthfully with investigations.

countryAddenda.us: SOX 806 protects reports of securities, mail, wire or bank fraud or SEC-rule violations to supervisors or agencies (OSHA complaint within 180 days; pre-dispute arbitration does not apply), while Dodd-Frank anti-retaliation (double back pay) requires a report to the SEC (Digital Realty v. Somers, 2018). Audit every template (offer letter, PIIA, separation agreement, investigation scripts) for Rule 21F-17 compliance and carve SOX claims out of arbitration agreements.
countryAddenda.us-ca: Labor Code 1102.5 protects internal and external reports of any suspected legal violation (penalty up to $10,000 per violation), and SB 497 creates a rebuttable presumption of retaliation for adverse action within 90 days of protected activity. Post the Labor Commissioner whistleblower hotline notice (LC 1102.8) and require Legal review of any adverse action inside the 90-day window.
countryAddenda.ca: Add Criminal Code s.425.1 (retaliating against employees who report offences to authorities is a crime) and the ESA s.74 and OHSA s.50 reprisal prohibitions; in BC protect pay discussions and pay-transparency complaints (Pay Transparency Act s.4). Hotline data is personal information under BC PIPA (reasonable purpose and notice) and protected in Ontario by the intrusion-upon-seclusion tort, so disclose the vendor and data location.
countryAddenda.in: The Companies Act s.177(9)-(10) vigil mechanism is mandatory only for listed companies or those with public deposits or borrowings over INR 50 crore; otherwise the global hotline serves as the vigil mechanism. Route sexual-harassment complaints to the POSH Internal Committee and worker grievances to the Grievance Redressal Committee (20+ workers; 30-day resolution), and bring hotline processing within DPDP notice and security duties by 13 May 2027.
countryAddenda.tw: Route sexual-harassment complaints to the GEEA channel (10+ employees) and workplace-bullying complaints to the OSH Act bullying channel (from 1 July 2026), each with statutory investigation and authority-notification steps. LSA Art. 74 bars dismissal, demotion or pay cuts for reporting labor-law violations to the employer or authorities; give a PDPA notice for hotline data.
countryAddenda.cn: Anonymous reporting is permitted, but hotline and investigation data sent to US systems or vendors requires a PIPL notice, separate consent (or a documented HR-management basis) and a PIPIA, so prefer a China-hosted intake instance. Brief investigators on Counter-Espionage Law and Data Security Law sensitivities before evidence leaves China, and on Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law exposure where reports concern US export-control compliance.

decisions: Third-party hotline vendor vs. in-house intake? (A vendor provides independence and anonymous two-way messaging auditors expect; confirm data-residency options for China and India.)
Allow anonymous reports in every country? (Yes in practice across the footprint; configure anonymous follow-up so investigators can ask questions.)

Who investigates what? (Common split: Ethics & Compliance/Legal for fraud, bribery, export and securities; Employee Relations for harassment and conduct; outside counsel for executive or Audit Committee matters.)
Retaliation monitoring period: 12 or 24 months? (Longer if a RIF or reorganization is planned.)
Require managers to log every concern they receive in the case system? (Improves Audit Committee reporting and retaliation defense, but needs training to avoid logging routine grievances.)
Recognize or reward reporters? (Most issuers avoid cash awards; confidential thanks is safer.)
pitfalls: Separation agreements requiring departing employees to waive SEC whistleblower awards or notify the Company before contacting regulators (seven companies charged in Sept 2024; Foot Locker in May 2026).
Managers investigating concerns themselves or confronting the accused before Employee Relations is engaged, contaminating evidence and signaling retaliation.
Taking adverse action soon after a report without a documented protected-activity check, especially inside California's 90-day presumption window.
Slow triage of export-control or FCPA reports, forfeiting the 120-day self-disclosure credit.
Moving China hotline data to US servers without PIPL separate consent and a PIPIA.
policies.training: Speak Up and non-retaliation content in Code training at hire and annually; manager module on receiving concerns and retaliation risk at promotion and every 2 years; annual training for investigators.

policies.name: Conflicts of Interest & Outside Activities
policies.owner: Ethics & Compliance (disclosure program), with Legal (related-person transactions) and HR (outside-employment approvals)
policies.approver: General Counsel + CHRO; Audit Committee (or other independent committee) for related-person transactions under Item 404
policies.review: Annual; update when outbound-investment or foreign-talent rules change
policies.audience: All employees, officers and directors; contractors with access to confidential information
policies.purpose: Requires employees to disclose and manage personal interests that could compromise, or appear to compromise, their judgment for the Company, including outside employment, investments, advisory roles and relationships with customers, suppliers and competitors. For a chip company it also covers foreign talent programs, investments in China-based semiconductor and AI companies (US outbound investment rules) and side projects that put IP ownership at risk.
keyProvisions: Employees must disclose actual, potential and perceived conflicts in the COI module within 30 days of hire, during annual certification and within 10 business days of any change.

Written pre-approval from the employee's VP and Ethics & Compliance is required before any outside employment, consulting or advisory role in semiconductors, EDA, electronics or AI, or with any customer, supplier, foundry, OSAT, distributor or competitor; before joining a for-profit board; and before founding a company.

Without approval, employees may not hold any interest in a private company that is a customer, supplier or competitor, or more than 1% of the shares of such a public company; diversified mutual and index funds are excluded.

Employees must disclose any application to, invitation to or participation in a government-sponsored foreign talent recruitment program; participation in a malign foreign talent recruitment program is prohibited for anyone working on federally funded R&D.

US persons must obtain Legal review before making, or directing, any equity investment, advisory-for-equity arrangement or joint venture involving a company in China, Hong Kong or Macau active in semiconductors, AI or quantum, because 31 CFR Part 850 may prohibit it or require notice to Treasury within 30 days.

Transactions over $120,000 in which the Company participates and a director, executive officer, 5%+ holder or their immediate family member has a material interest require prior Audit Committee approval (Item 404; Nasdaq 5630).

Company time, EDA licenses, lab equipment, design data and confidential information may not be used for outside activities; inventions relating to the Company's business or R&D remain subject to the invention-assignment agreement.
Employees may not accept personal benefits (gifts, loans, preferential investment allocations) from customers, suppliers or distributors except as permitted under the Anti-Bribery policy thresholds.
Employees must recuse themselves from hiring, procurement, pricing and design-win decisions in which they or a relative have an interest.
Ethics & Compliance records each decision (approve, approve with conditions, decline), with conditions such as recusal, information barriers or time limits, and re-reviews approvals annually.
Disclosure rules apply uniformly regardless of nationality or national origin; disclosed information is used only to manage conflicts.
Undisclosed conflicts are Code violations and are escalated to Legal and Security where they involve possible trade-secret or export-control risk.
policies.sampleLanguage:
Your Duty to Disclose. You must act in the best interests of [Company] and avoid situations where your personal interests conflict, or appear to conflict, with your responsibilities. Disclose any actual or potential conflict in the COI portal within 30 days of joining, each year during annual certification, and within 10 business days whenever your circumstances change.

Activities Requiring Pre-Approval. You must obtain written approval from your Vice President and Ethics & Compliance before you: (a) work, consult or advise for any company in the semiconductor, EDA, electronics or AI industries, or for any customer, supplier or competitor of [Company]; (b) join the board of a for-profit company; (c) start a business; or (d) apply to or participate in any government-sponsored talent recruitment program. If you are a US person, you must also obtain Legal review before investing in or advising any China-, Hong Kong- or Macau-based company working in semiconductors, AI or quantum computing.

Use of Company Resources. You may not use Company time, tools, software licenses, equipment or confidential information for outside activities. Approval of an outside activity does not change your obligations under your confidentiality and invention assignment agreement.

roles.duties: Disclose conflicts on time, obtain pre-approval before outside roles or covered investments, and recuse from affected decisions.
Review team disclosures for business impact, enforce recusals and escalate suspected undisclosed conflicts.
Runs the annual certification, decides disclosures with Legal, maintains the COI register and re-reviews approvals annually.
Reviews outbound-investment, foreign talent program and related-person transaction issues and prepares Item 404 disclosure.
Assess red flags such as startup founding, talent-plan applications or ties to Entity List companies for insider and export risk.

countryAddenda.us: Align the related-person procedure with Item 404(b) and Nasdaq 5630 (independent review of transactions over $120,000). If the Company holds federal R&D awards, covered individuals must certify non-participation in malign foreign talent recruitment programs (CHIPS and Science Act s.10632; verify applicability).
countryAddenda.us-ca: Labor Code 96(k) and 98.6 bar adverse action for lawful off-duty conduct, so restrict outside work only where it competes with Company business, uses Company resources or puts confidential information at risk. Invention restrictions must respect LC 2870 (inventions developed entirely on the employee's own time without Company equipment or trade secrets, and unrelated to the business, are excluded).
countryAddenda.ca: Limits on outside work must be reasonable and tied to legitimate interests, or they risk being read as restraints of trade; senior technical leaders may owe fiduciary duties that support stricter rules. Canada has no statutory employee-invention regime, so rely on the express invention assignment and prior-inventions schedule for side projects.
countryAddenda.in: In-term exclusivity and anti-moonlighting clauses are enforceable because Contract Act s.27 does not bar restraints during employment; require disclosure of directorships, startup investments and side ventures. Resident employees' overseas investments follow FEMA ODI rules and must be reported in Schedule FA (verify thresholds).
countryAddenda.tw: Build outside-activity approval into the filed work rules so breaches can be disciplined, and require disclosure of any role with PRC-linked entities given National Security Act and Cross-Strait Act enforcement (MJIB questioned 114 people in 2026 talent-poaching probes). Staff on government-commissioned core key technology projects must disclose mainland China travel, which requires approval, including after departure (Cross-Strait Act Art. 9).
countryAddenda.cn: Incorporate the disclosure duty into the democratically adopted handbook; LCL Art. 39(4) permits dismissal where concurrent employment with another employer seriously affects work or the employee refuses to end it after being told. Collect disclosure data under the PIPL employee notice and route outbound-investment questions for US-person staff in China to Legal.

decisions: Investment materiality threshold: any private stake plus 1% of a public customer, supplier or competitor, or a dollar threshold? (Lower thresholds raise volume; always exclude diversified funds.)
Blanket pre-approval for teaching, unrelated open source and non-profit boards? (Cuts volume; keep semiconductor-related open source and IP-sensitive topics in scope.)
Approver for outside work: manager only vs. VP + Ethics & Compliance? (VP + E&C for industry-related roles; manager for unrelated part-time work.)

Family-member scope: spouse/partner and household only, or relatives at customers, suppliers and government bodies too? (Broader scope supports FCPA and Item 404 but raises privacy concerns in China and India.)
Combine COI disclosure with annual Code certification or run a separate campaign? (Combining improves completion; separate campaigns improve data quality.)
pitfalls: Collecting disclosures but never deciding or re-reviewing them, so an approval goes stale while the employee's side venture pivots into a competing field.
Treating Chinese or Taiwanese nationality as a proxy for risk instead of applying disclosure rules uniformly (Title VII, 8 U.S.C. 1324b and Canadian human rights exposure).
Missing that an executive's outside board seat or a relative's vendor contract is a related-person transaction or a Code waiver requiring Audit Committee or Board action.
Blanket bans on all outside work for California employees that conflict with Labor Code 96(k).
Allowing advisory-for-equity roles in Chinese chip or AI startups without an outbound-investment review.
policies.training: COI module at hire and annual certification; targeted briefing for engineering leaders, corporate development and executives on outbound-investment and foreign talent program rules every year.

policies.name: Anti-Bribery & Anti-Corruption (HR aspects)
policies.owner: Ethics & Compliance (ABAC program); Talent Acquisition and Employee Relations own the HR controls
policies.approver: General Counsel + CHRO; Audit Committee oversight of the ABAC program
policies.review: Annual; after enforcement-policy changes or any high-risk hiring exception
policies.audience: All employees, with enhanced controls for Talent Acquisition, hiring managers, University Programs, Sales, FAEs, country GMs and executives
policies.purpose: Prevents jobs, internships, referrals, gifts and hospitality from being used to obtain or reward business, especially with government officials, state-owned customers, foundries, labs and universities. It applies the FCPA anti-bribery and books-and-records provisions that bind the Company as a US issuer, together with local anti-corruption laws in China, India, Taiwan and Canada, to HR-controlled decisions.
keyProvisions: No one may offer or give employment, internships, referrals, training, gifts, travel or any other thing of value to a government official, an employee of a state-owned enterprise, or a customer employee (or any of their relatives) to obtain, retain or reward business or secure an improper advantage.

Every application and referral in Greenhouse asks whether the candidate or a close relative is a government official, SOE employee, or employee of a current or prospective customer, supplier or university partner; any 'yes' routes the candidate to Ethics & Compliance before an offer.
Candidates connected to officials or customer decision-makers must go through the standard process against a documented scorecard; no role may be created, criteria waived or pay adjusted for them.

Internships and fellowships are filled by open application only; the Company does not accept customer-, government- or partner-requested placements, and such requests are reported to Ethics & Compliance.

Gifts and hospitality to or from employees of customers, SOEs or government bodies must be modest, infrequent and recorded; anything above USD 100 (or a lower local limit) needs pre-approval, and cash or cash equivalents are prohibited.
Facilitation payments are prohibited, including to expedite work permits, visas, registrations or inspections; immigration, relocation and payroll agents must certify the same.

HR vendors that interact with officials (immigration counsel, relocation firms, social-insurance agents, labor-dispatch agencies) are screened, contracted with ABAC and audit clauses, and reviewed every 2 years.
Hiring files for flagged candidates, including business justification and approvals, are retained for at least 5 years.
Sales and FAE incentive plans give no credit for business obtained in breach of this policy, and amounts paid are subject to forfeiture and clawback.
Managers and high-risk roles complete ABAC training annually with certification.
Suspected violations are reported under the Speak Up policy and escalated to the General Counsel within 24 hours.
policies.sampleLanguage:
Hiring and Anti-Corruption. [Company] hires on merit. We never offer a job, internship, referral bonus, training opportunity or any other benefit to a government official, an employee of a state-owned enterprise, a customer or a relative of any of them in order to win or keep business or obtain any improper advantage. This rule applies even if the request comes from the customer, the official or a colleague.

When you apply or refer a candidate, you must disclose whether the candidate or a close family member works for a government body, state-owned company, university partner, customer or supplier with which [Company] does business. Ethics & Compliance will review every such disclosure before an offer is made, and the candidate will be assessed through the same process and criteria as every other applicant.

[Company] does not accept requests from customers, officials or partners to place interns or employees. Internship positions are filled only through open application.

Gifts and hospitality to or from customer or government personnel must be modest, infrequent, transparent and recorded. Anything valued above USD 100 requires advance approval, and cash or gift cards are never permitted.

roles.duties: Runs the relationship question in Greenhouse, holds flagged candidates until Compliance clears them and documents merit-based selection.
Reviews flagged candidates and gift requests within 5 business days, audits hiring files and delivers ABAC training.
Assess every candidate against the same scorecard and never create roles or adjust criteria for connected candidates.
Advises on FCPA and local anti-bribery laws and on self-disclosure decisions.
Report customer placement requests and make sure incentive plans and customer interactions follow ABAC rules.

countryAddenda.us: The FCPA anti-bribery and accounting provisions (15 U.S.C. 78dd-1, 78m(b)) apply to the Company as an issuer; the SEC fined Qualcomm $7.5M (2016) for 'must place' hires of Chinese officials' relatives. DOJ's June 9, 2025 guidelines narrowed enforcement priorities, but the statute, SEC books-and-records enforcement and limitation periods are unchanged, and the Foreign Extortion Prevention Act reaches officials who demand bribes.
countryAddenda.us-ca: No addendum needed; global policy suffices.
countryAddenda.ca: The Corruption of Foreign Public Officials Act applies to the Canadian subsidiary and its employees, and Criminal Code s.426 (secret commissions) covers private-sector bribery (verify current penalties). Screen university research partners and Mitacs interns under the federal Policy on Sensitive Technology Research and Affiliations of Concern.
countryAddenda.in: Prevention of Corruption Act 1988 s.9 (2018 amendment) makes the company liable for undue advantages given to public servants unless it proves 'adequate procedures', so keep this policy, training records and a gifts register. Treat PSU customers, government labs and state universities as public-sector counterparties and document merit selection for any connected candidate.
countryAddenda.tw: Bribery of Taiwan public officials, including personnel of state-owned enterprises and public research institutes, is criminal under the Anti-Corruption Act; private commercial bribery is addressed mainly through Criminal Code breach-of-trust provisions (verify). Apply the relationship question to candidates connected to government-funded projects and state-owned customers.
countryAddenda.cn: Commercial bribery is prohibited under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law (revised, effective 15 Oct 2025) and the Criminal Law, covering gifts, hospitality, customer travel and hiring favors for customer or SOE personnel. List ABAC breaches as 'serious violations' in the democratically adopted handbook so LCL Art. 39 dismissal is available, and screen labor-dispatch and HR agencies.

decisions: Gift and hospitality limits: one global USD 100 threshold or lower local limits for SOE customers in China and India? (Lower limits reduce risk but add approvals.)
Relationship question scope: all government officials, or only those connected to Company business? (Broad capture with a fast clearance step is common.)
Pay referral bonuses for candidates referred by customers or officials? (Most issuers prohibit them.)
Central vs. regional review of flagged candidates? (Central review is more consistent; regional review is faster during China and India hiring surges.)
What happens when Compliance review exceeds its SLA: hold the offer or release it? (Set a 5-business-day SLA and escalate rather than release uncleared offers.)
pitfalls: Creating 'special' internships or summer roles for customer executives' children, often at the request of sales.
Assuming the 2025 FCPA enforcement reset means hiring-related bribery is no longer pursued; SEC books-and-records rules and local laws still apply.
Paying immigration or relocation agents who make undocumented 'expediting' payments to officials.
Not keeping hiring files for flagged candidates, leaving no evidence of merit-based selection.
policies.training: ABAC training at hire for all employees; annual training and certification for TA, hiring managers, Sales, FAEs, University Programs and country GMs.

policies.name: Insider Trading
policies.owner: Legal (Securities) with Equity Administration (Stock Admin)
policies.approver: Board of Directors (policy filed as Form 10-K Exhibit 19); General Counsel for administrative procedures and designations
policies.review: Annual; also on any change in reporting cadence (e.g., an election to report semiannually) or SEC rules
policies.audience: All directors, officers, employees, contractors and consultants worldwide, their family and household members, and entities they control
policies.purpose: Prohibits trading on material nonpublic information (MNPI) and tipping, sets quarterly blackout windows, pre-clearance and Rule 10b5-1 plan rules, and bans hedging and pledging. The policy is disclosed under Item 408(b) and filed as Exhibit 19, and protects employees, including engineers and sales staff who see design wins, tape-out results and customer forecasts, from inadvertent violations.
keyProvisions: No one may buy, sell, gift or otherwise transact in [Company] securities while aware of MNPI, or pass MNPI to others or recommend trades (tipping); the same prohibition applies to securities of customers, suppliers, foundry and OSAT partners, competitors and acquisition targets ('shadow trading').

MNPI includes unannounced financial results or guidance, design wins or losses, tape-out and qualification results, customer forecasts and ramps, supply constraints, export-license outcomes, M&A, RIFs and executive changes.

Quarterly blackout: Designated Insiders may not trade from the 15th day of the last month of each fiscal quarter until one full trading day after the earnings release; the General Counsel may impose event-specific blackouts at any time without explanation.

Designated Insiders (directors, officers, finance, legal, IR and employees designated by role, such as product and sales leaders with forecast or design-win access) must pre-clear every transaction with Legal; clearance is valid for 2 trading days.

Rule 10b5-1 plans may be adopted or modified only in an open window after pre-clearance, and must meet the cooling-off period (directors and officers: later of 90 days or 2 business days after the 10-Q/10-K for the quarter of adoption, capped at 120 days; others: 30 days), with no overlapping plans and no more than one single-trade plan in 12 months.

Hedging (collars, swaps, forwards, exchange funds), short sales, trading in puts, calls or other derivatives on [Company] securities, pledging and holding [Company] securities in margin accounts are prohibited for all directors, officers and employees.

Directors and Section 16 officers pre-clear all transactions and report executed trades to Legal the same day so Form 4s are filed within 2 business days; affiliates also comply with Rule 144 and Form 144 filing.

Sell-to-cover for RSU tax withholding under a standing instruction, ESPP purchases under standing elections and cash exercises of options are permitted during blackouts; sales of the acquired shares are not.
HR notifies Legal the same day an employee is hired into, promoted into or leaves a Designated Insider or Section 16 role; Equity Administration enforces blocks through the plan broker.
The policy continues to apply after employment ends while the person holds MNPI, and departing Designated Insiders remain subject to any blackout in effect on their last day.
Employees acknowledge the policy at hire and certify annually; the policy is available in Simplified and Traditional Chinese.
Violations result in discipline up to termination and may be referred to authorities.
policies.sampleLanguage:
Prohibition on Insider Trading. If you are aware of material nonpublic information about [Company], you may not buy, sell, gift or otherwise trade in [Company] securities, and you may not share that information with anyone else or recommend that they trade. The same rule applies to information you learn through your work about our customers, suppliers, foundry and packaging partners, competitors or potential acquisition targets. Information is 'material' if a reasonable investor would consider it important, such as unannounced revenue, design wins or losses, tape-out results, customer forecasts, export-license decisions or executive changes.

Trading Windows. If you are a Designated Insider, you may trade only during an open window, which begins one full trading day after our quarterly earnings release and ends on the 15th day of the last month of the fiscal quarter, and only after you obtain pre-clearance from Legal. Legal may close the window at any time.

Prohibited Transactions. No director, officer or employee may engage in short sales, trade options or other derivatives on [Company] securities, hedge their ownership of [Company] securities, or pledge [Company] securities as collateral.

Continuing Obligation. These restrictions continue after your employment ends for as long as you possess material nonpublic information.

roles.duties: Maintains the policy and Designated Insider list, runs pre-clearance, approves 10b5-1 plans and prepares Form 4 and Item 408 disclosures.
Enforces blackout blocks and 10b5-1 plan terms with the broker and sends grant, vest and withholding data to Legal within one business day.
Notifies Legal the same day of hires, promotions and exits that change insider status, and collects acknowledgments.
Nominate team members with MNPI access (design wins, forecasts, tape-outs) for designation and reinforce event-specific blackouts.
Never trade or tip while aware of MNPI, pre-clear when designated and certify annually.

countryAddenda.us: Item 408(a) requires quarterly disclosure of director and officer 10b5-1 plan adoptions and terminations, Item 407(i) requires disclosure of hedging policies, and Section 16(b) short-swing profits are recoverable on a strict-liability basis. Track the SEC's May 2026 optional semiannual (Form 10-S) proposal, which would change window timing and 10b5-1 cooling-off calculations if adopted and elected.
countryAddenda.us-ca: No addendum needed; global policy suffices.
countryAddenda.ca: Canadian insider-trading and tipping rules apply to securities of Canadian reporting issuers, so the global policy is the operative standard for [Company] shares; extend shadow-trading reminders to any Canadian-listed customers or partners (verify). Provide a French version for any Quebec-based employee.
countryAddenda.in: Employees must report foreign shares acquired through RSUs or ESPP in Schedule FA of their income-tax return, and ESPP purchases are subject to FEMA/LRS rules. SEBI insider trading regulations apply to Indian-listed securities, so the shadow-trading rule covers Indian-listed customers and partners (verify).
countryAddenda.tw: Provide a Traditional Chinese version and extend the shadow-trading rule expressly to Taiwan-listed customers, foundries and OSATs whose performance employees see through supply-chain work, where Securities and Exchange Act Art. 157-1 insider-trading prohibitions apply (verify).
countryAddenda.cn: Employees trade only through the SAFE Circular 7 registered plan and designated broker, and sale proceeds must be repatriated through the special FX account controlled by Equity Administration. Provide a Chinese version, and transfer broker and pre-clearance data to the US only under PIPL notice and separate consent.

decisions: Blackout start: the 15th of the last fiscal month, two weeks before quarter-end, or quarter-end? (Earlier starts cut risk but shrink employees' windows.)

Designated Insiders beyond Section 16 officers: finance and legal only, or role-based designation of engineers and sales leaders with forecast and design-win access? (Role-based designation fits semiconductor MNPI patterns.)
Pre-clearance for all employees or Designated Insiders only? (Designated Insiders only is standard at 1,500-5,000 employees.)
Require Section 16 officers to sell only under 10b5-1 plans? (Common best practice; reduces litigation exposure.)
Shadow-trading scope: a maintained list of named partners and competitors, or a general principle? (A named list is clearer but must be kept current.)
Window design if the Company elects semiannual reporting? (Keep windows keyed to earnings releases if quarterly releases continue.)
pitfalls: Stale Designated Insider lists that miss newly promoted product and sales leaders who see design wins and customer forecasts.
Ignoring shadow trading in customers' and foundry partners' stock after the SEC v. Panuwat verdict (2024).
Letting officers modify 10b5-1 plans without recognizing that a modification restarts the cooling-off period.
Late Form 4s because HR does not tell Legal about officer appointments or vest data arrives late.
No translated policy or live training in Asia, where engineers hold substantial RSU positions.
policies.training: Acknowledgment at hire; annual certification; quarterly window-opening and blackout notices; live training for Designated Insiders and new Section 16 officers at onboarding.

policies.name: Compensation Recovery (Clawback)
policies.owner: Total Rewards with Legal and Finance (Controller)
policies.approver: Compensation Committee of the Board; policy filed as Form 10-K Exhibit 97
policies.review: Annual; immediately upon any restatement or rule change
policies.audience: Mandatory recovery: current and former executive officers (Rule 16a-1(f) officers); discretionary misconduct recovery: all recipients of incentive compensation, including equity
policies.purpose: Implements the mandatory, no-fault recovery of erroneously awarded incentive compensation after an accounting restatement required by Rule 10D-1 and Nasdaq Rule 5608, and adds a discretionary right to recover pay for misconduct (including export-control, fraud and trade-secret violations) that goes beyond the mandatory rule. It makes recovery enforceable across pay instruments and countries.
keyProvisions: If the Company is required to prepare an accounting restatement (a 'Big R' restatement or a 'little r' revision), the Compensation Committee will recover, reasonably promptly and regardless of fault, the pre-tax amount of incentive-based compensation received by any current or former executive officer during the three completed fiscal years before the date the restatement was required that exceeds what would have been received on the restated results.

Incentive-based compensation means any compensation granted, earned or vested based wholly or partly on a financial reporting measure, including stock price and TSR (e.g., annual bonus funded on revenue or non-GAAP operating margin, PSUs, TSR awards); time-based RSUs and discretionary bonuses not tied to financial measures are outside mandatory recovery.

For stock-price or TSR measures, the recoverable amount is a reasonable estimate of the restatement's effect using a methodology approved in advance with the independent compensation consultant, with documentation retained for Nasdaq.
The Company will not indemnify, insure or reimburse any executive officer for recovered amounts, and no plan, agreement or separation arrangement may override this policy.

Recovery may be pursued by repayment demand, cancellation or forfeiture of unvested or unpaid awards, offset against future compensation where lawful, or legal action; recovery may be forgone only where impracticable under the narrow Rule 10D-1 exceptions, as determined by the independent Compensation Committee.

Discretionary misconduct recovery: the Committee (for executives) or the CHRO and General Counsel (for other employees) may recover or cancel incentive and equity compensation paid or vested in the 3 years before discovery where the employee committed fraud, willful misconduct, a violation of export-control, sanctions or anti-bribery law, theft or misuse of trade secrets, or a material Code breach causing financial or reputational harm, or knowingly failed as a supervisor to prevent such conduct.

Every executive officer signs a clawback acknowledgment at appointment; all incentive plans, award agreements, offer letters and severance or change-in-control agreements incorporate this policy by reference.
Total Rewards keeps a register of executive officers and, for at least 3 years after payment, the metrics, calculations and payouts for each incentive award so they can be recalculated.
The Company discloses recovery analyses under Item 402(w) and files this policy as Exhibit 97; failure to adopt, disclose or enforce it can lead to delisting under Nasdaq 5608.
Recovery from employees outside the US is carried out in line with local wage-deduction and labor laws, using award cancellation where deductions are not permitted.
policies.sampleLanguage:
Mandatory Recovery. If [Company] is required to prepare an accounting restatement due to material noncompliance with any financial reporting requirement under the securities laws, including a restatement to correct an error that would result in a material misstatement if left uncorrected in the current period, the Compensation Committee shall recover, reasonably promptly, the Erroneously Awarded Compensation received by any current or former Executive Officer during the three completed fiscal years immediately preceding the date on which the Company is required to prepare the restatement. Recovery is required whether or not the Executive Officer engaged in misconduct or was responsible for the restatement. Erroneously Awarded Compensation is the amount of Incentive-Based Compensation received that exceeds the amount that would have been received had it been determined based on the restated amounts, computed without regard to any taxes paid.

No Indemnification. [Company] shall not indemnify any Executive Officer against the loss of Erroneously Awarded Compensation or pay premiums on any insurance policy covering such loss.

Misconduct Recovery. In addition, the Committee may, in its discretion, require any Covered Employee to repay or forfeit incentive or equity compensation received during the three years before the discovery of Misconduct, as defined in this Policy.

roles.duties: Approves the policy, determines recoverable amounts and impracticability, and exercises discretion on misconduct recovery for executives.
Maintains the executive register and award calculation records, embeds the policy in plans and agreements and executes recovery.
Identifies restatement triggers, recalculates financial measures and supports the TSR or stock-price effect estimate.
Advises on recovery mechanics and local-law limits and prepares Item 402(w) disclosure and the Exhibit 97 filing.
Cancel unvested awards, process repayments and correct tax reporting across entities.

countryAddenda.us: Mandatory recovery is calculated pre-tax, so coordinate with Tax on employees' treatment of repaid amounts taxed in prior years (verify). Separation, severance and change-in-control agreements must not release or indemnify clawback obligations, and check Section 409A before offsetting against deferred compensation.
countryAddenda.us-ca: Do not recover through payroll deductions: Labor Code 221 and 224 bar deductions except as authorized, and final wages cannot be offset. Recover by written demand or cancellation of unvested awards, and frame recovery around restatement or misconduct, not departure, because AB 692 bars repayment obligations triggered by separation for agreements from 1 Jan 2026 (confirm with counsel).
countryAddenda.ca: Deductions from wages require written authorization and statutory permission under the ON and BC ESAs, so recover by demand or award cancellation, and draft forfeiture and recovery terms clearly because courts read equity forfeiture language strictly (Matthews v. Ocean Nutrition, 2020 SCC 26). Confirm with Tax whether repayments of previously taxed amounts are deductible (verify).
countryAddenda.in: Deductions are limited to authorized items within 50% of wages (Code on Wages s.18), so recover by demand, cancellation of unvested RSUs or contractual set-off where clearly agreed; recovery terms must be a reasonable pre-estimate rather than a penalty (Contract Act s.74). TDS already deducted on perquisites is not automatically refunded (verify).
countryAddenda.tw: LSA Art. 26 prohibits pre-deducting damages or penalties from wages, so recover by separate demand or cancellation of unvested equity; build the clawback into award agreements signed by the employee and, for misconduct-linked recovery, into the work rules.
countryAddenda.cn: Deductions for employee-caused losses are capped at 20% of monthly wage and cannot reduce pay below minimum wage, and LCL Art. 25 limits employee liquidated damages to service-period and non-compete clauses, so cash clawback is difficult. Rely mainly on forfeiture of unvested awards under the SAFE-registered plan terms (verify enforceability with local counsel).

decisions: Scope of discretionary misconduct recovery: executive officers only or all equity recipients? (Broader scope earns DOJ compliance-program credit but is harder to enforce outside the US.)
Lookback for misconduct recovery: 3 years or unlimited? (3 years mirrors Rule 10D-1 and eases enforcement.)
Include 'failure to supervise' as a trigger for managers of wrongdoers? (DOJ credits it; needs a clear definition.)
Pre-agree the TSR and stock-price impact methodology with the consultant? (Recommended; reduces disputes and Nasdaq documentation risk.)
Recovery order across instruments: cash bonus first or unvested equity first? (Cancelling unvested equity first is simplest globally.)
pitfalls: An executive-officer list that omits former officers or Rule 16a-1(f) officers such as the principal accounting officer.
Separation or D&O arrangements that indemnify or insure recovered amounts, which Rule 10D-1 prohibits.
No retained award calculations, making restated recalculation impossible.
Attempting payroll deductions in California, Taiwan or China in breach of wage-payment laws.
policies.training: Signed acknowledgment by each executive officer at appointment; annual Compensation Committee briefing; award agreements carry the policy reference for all other participants.

policies.name: Workplace Relationships & Employment of Relatives
policies.owner: HR (Employee Relations)
policies.approver: CHRO + General Counsel
policies.review: Every 2 years + on law change
policies.audience: All employees, interns and contractors; directors and executive officers for related-person aspects
policies.purpose: Manages the conflict-of-interest, favoritism, harassment and segregation-of-duties risks that arise when employees are in close personal relationships with, or are related to, colleagues they supervise or influence. It sets disclosure and reporting-line rules and aligns hiring of relatives with SEC related-person disclosure and anti-corruption controls.
keyProvisions: Employees must disclose to HR within 10 business days any romantic, sexual or family relationship with another employee or contractor where either can influence the other's hiring, pay, performance rating, promotion, work assignments or access rights.

No employee may directly or indirectly supervise, rate, set pay for, approve expenses of, or audit a relative or partner; HR resolves conflicts by changing reporting lines or responsibilities, choosing the least disruptive option and never defaulting to moving the more junior person.
Romantic or sexual relationships between an executive officer (or any member of the CEO's staff) and any employee in their organization are prohibited.

Relatives (spouse or partner, parents, children, siblings, in-laws, grandparents, grandchildren and household members) may be hired only if they will not report into, or sit in the approval chain of, the related employee, and the related employee takes no part in selection.
Hiring an immediate family member of a director or executive officer requires Legal review and prior Audit Committee approval; pay above $120,000 is disclosed under Item 404.
Candidates related to government officials or customer personnel are handled under the Anti-Bribery policy.

Relationships between people in segregated roles (payroll input and approval, stock administration and Section 16 officers, trade compliance and license applicants, security and investigated employees) must be disclosed so segregation of duties is preserved.
Disclosures are confidential, stored separately from general personnel files and used only to manage conflicts; the Company does not otherwise regulate lawful personal relationships.
Unwelcome conduct after a relationship ends, or pressure to start one, is handled under the Anti-Harassment policy; failure by a supervisor to disclose is a disciplinary matter up to termination.
HR re-checks disclosed relationships at each reorganization, promotion or transfer.
policies.sampleLanguage:
Disclosure. [Company] respects employees' private lives and does not prohibit personal relationships between colleagues. However, relationships between people who work together can create conflicts of interest, perceptions of favoritism and harassment risk. If you are in a romantic or family relationship with another employee or contractor, and either of you can influence the other's hiring, pay, performance evaluation, promotion, work assignments or access rights, you must disclose the relationship to HR within ten business days. Disclosures are kept confidential and shared only with those who need to know to resolve the conflict.

Reporting Lines. No employee may supervise, evaluate, set compensation for or approve transactions of a relative or partner. If a conflict exists, HR will work with both employees to change reporting lines or responsibilities. Executive officers may not have a romantic or sexual relationship with any employee in their organization.

Hiring Relatives. Relatives of current employees may apply for positions and will be assessed on merit, but the related employee may not participate in the hiring decision, and the new hire may not report within the related employee's chain of approval.

roles.duties: Disclose covered relationships within 10 business days and recuse from decisions affecting the other person.
Report known undisclosed relationships affecting their team and implement reporting-line changes.
Receives disclosures confidentially, designs mitigations and re-checks them at reorganizations.
Reviews hires of directors' and executive officers' relatives for Item 404 and Audit Committee approval.
Asks the relationship question in Greenhouse and keeps related employees off hiring panels.

countryAddenda.us: Apply the rules neutrally to avoid marital-status and sex-discrimination claims under state laws (verify state list), and make sure disclosure rules do not restrict NLRA Section 7 activity. Put the executive relationship prohibition into executive offer letters as a 'cause' ground.
countryAddenda.us-ca: FEHA protects marital status, and restrictions on spouses or registered domestic partners working in the same department or supervisory line must rest on bona fide business reasons such as supervision, safety, security or morale (FEHA marital-status regulations; verify citation). Give CCPA notice for relationship data and keep it separate from personnel files.
countryAddenda.ca: Marital and family status are protected grounds in Ontario and BC; the Ontario Human Rights Code s.24(1)(d) permits an employer to refuse to employ or promote a spouse, child or parent of an employee, while BC restrictions should be justified as bona fide occupational requirements (verify). Handle post-relationship harassment under the Ontario OHSA and WorkSafeBC programs.
countryAddenda.in: No statute regulates workplace relationships; incorporate the policy into service rules. A complaint by a woman arising from a supervisor relationship must go to the POSH Internal Committee, and disclosure data is handled under the SPDI Rules (DPDP from 13 May 2027).
countryAddenda.tw: Include disclosure and reporting-line rules in the filed work rules; the 2023 GEEA amendments impose heavier liability for power-based sexual harassment by supervisors, so enforce the supervisor-subordinate rule strictly. Relationship data is personal data under the PDPA and needs notice.
countryAddenda.cn: Adopt the policy through democratic procedure and define non-disclosure as a violation; reassigning either partner to another department or city needs consent where it changes contract terms (LCL Art. 35). Collect relationship data under the PIPL employee notice.

decisions: Supervisor-subordinate relationships: disclosure plus reporting-line change, or outright prohibition? (Disclosure is common for managers; prohibition for executive officers.)
Which person changes role when a conflict arises? (Decide jointly with both employees, weighting business need, to avoid sex-discrimination risk.)
How broadly to define 'relative' (household members, in-laws, cousins)? (Broad definitions support Item 404 and FCPA controls; narrower ones are easier to administer.)
Allow relatives on the same team if not in the same reporting line? (Often allowed, but restricted in finance, payroll, trade compliance and security.)
Consequence for non-disclosure: warning or termination for executives? (Termination-for-cause language for officers is increasingly common.)
pitfalls: Routinely transferring the more junior partner, often a woman, creating sex-discrimination exposure.
Missing Item 404 disclosure for a director's or executive officer's relative earning over $120,000.
Not re-checking conflicts after reorganizations, leaving a partner in the approval chain for pay or promotion.
Handling relationship disclosures like ordinary personnel data and oversharing them.
policies.training: Acknowledgment at hire and on material change; covered in people-manager training at promotion.

policies.name: Equal Employment Opportunity
policies.owner: HR (Employee Relations) with Employment Legal; Talent Acquisition for hiring practices
policies.approver: CHRO + General Counsel
policies.review: Annual + on law change (the US federal posture on DEI changed repeatedly in 2025-26)
policies.audience: All employees, applicants, interns, contractors and agency workers in every country
policies.purpose: Commits the Company to employment decisions based on job-related merit without discrimination on any ground protected where the employee works, and sets how accommodation, complaints and outcome monitoring work. It also aligns inclusion programs and public statements with the 2025-26 US federal posture, under which demographic-restricted programs create Title VII, Section 1981 and False Claims Act exposure, while keeping equality measures that local law requires.
keyProvisions: The Company prohibits discrimination in recruitment, hiring, pay, benefits, promotion, training, discipline, layoffs and termination on the basis of race, color, national origin, ancestry, citizenship or immigration status (where protected), religion or creed, caste, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital or family status, age, disability, genetic information, HIV or other health status, veteran status, or any other ground protected by applicable law.
Selection, pay, rating, promotion and RIF decisions use documented, job-related criteria (scorecards, calibrated ratings, job architecture), with the rationale recorded in Greenhouse or Darwinbox.

ERGs, mentoring, sponsorship, internships, fellowships, scholarships and events are open to all eligible employees or applicants; the Company does not use demographic hiring quotas, diverse-slate mandates or demographic-linked incentive metrics, except where local law requires a specific measure (e.g., Taiwan's disability employment quota).
Outreach may be broad (a wide range of universities, professional associations and communities) but may not exclude or prefer candidates because of a protected characteristic.
The Company provides reasonable accommodation for disability, pregnancy-related limitations, religion and other protected needs through the interactive process in the Reasonable Accommodation policy.
Export-control screening applies only to roles flagged for controlled technology and only to determine license needs; citizenship or national origin is never used as a hiring shortcut.
Discrimination complaints may be raised through any Speak Up channel and are investigated promptly and impartially; retaliation is prohibited.
Voluntary self-identification data is collected only where lawful, stored separately from personnel files, accessible only to HR Analytics and never used in individual decisions.

Legal reviews all external statements about workforce composition and inclusion (10-K human capital section, proxy, sustainability report, careers site) for accuracy and consistency with programs actually operated.
HR Analytics reviews hiring, promotion, pay, PIP, termination and RIF outcomes for adverse impact at least annually, and before each RIF, under attorney-client privilege.
Managers who discriminate, or who fail to escalate complaints, face corrective action up to termination.
policies.sampleLanguage:
Equal Opportunity. [Company] makes employment decisions based on job-related qualifications, performance and business needs. We do not discriminate against any applicant or employee on the basis of race, color, religion, creed, caste, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, age, disability, genetic information, marital or family status, veteran status or any other characteristic protected by law in the country where you work. This commitment applies to recruitment, hiring, compensation, benefits, training, promotion, transfer, discipline, layoff and termination.

Programs Open to All. Our employee resource groups, mentoring programs, internships and development programs are open to every employee or applicant who meets the job-related eligibility criteria. We do not set hiring quotas or make decisions based on protected characteristics, except where local law requires a specific measure.

Accommodation. We provide reasonable accommodation to qualified individuals with disabilities, for pregnancy-related limitations and for sincerely held religious beliefs, unless it would cause undue hardship.

Reporting. If you believe you have experienced or witnessed discrimination, report it through any channel in our Speak Up policy. We will investigate promptly and will not tolerate retaliation.

roles.duties: Own the policy, approve eligibility criteria for programs and review public inclusion statements.
Apply structured, job-related selection and remove unlawful questions and criteria from Greenhouse.
Make and document decisions on job-related criteria and escalate complaints immediately.
Runs privileged adverse-impact reviews of hiring, promotion, pay and RIF outcomes.
Investigates discrimination complaints and recommends corrective action.

countryAddenda.us: Cover Title VII, ADA, ADEA (20+), GINA, PWFA and Section 1981, and keep sexual orientation and gender identity protections (Bostock and state law) even though the EEOC rescinded its 2024 harassment guidance on Jan 22, 2026. EO 14173 revoked EO 11246 (OFCCP rescinded its regulations Aug 21, 2026) and requires federal contractors to certify no illegal DEI, creating False Claims Act exposure (IBM $17M settlement, Apr 10, 2026), and Ames v. Ohio (2025) eased majority-group claims. EEO-1 filing remains due until the July 2026 rescission proposal is final, and Section 503/VEVRAA duties apply if the Company holds covered federal contracts.
countryAddenda.us-ca: FEHA applies at 5+ employees and adds protected grounds (e.g., medical condition, reproductive health decision-making, military and veteran status); the EEO policy must be translated for any language spoken by 10%+ of a facility's workforce (2 CCR 11023). CRD automated-decision system rules (Oct 1, 2025) make the Company liable for discriminatory AI tools, including vendors', with 4-year data retention, and CRD pay data reporting continues regardless of EEO-1.
countryAddenda.ca: The Ontario and BC Human Rights Codes protect grounds including place of origin, citizenship (ON), creed, family status and record of offences (ON) or unrelated criminal conviction (BC), with a duty to accommodate to undue hardship and uncapped general damages. AODA requires accessible recruitment notices and accommodation in hiring; the Federal Contractors Program applies only with 100+ employees and a C$1M+ federal contract (verify).
countryAddenda.in: Publish an equal opportunity policy for persons with disabilities (RPwD Act s.21) and appoint a liaison officer (20+ employees); adopt a transgender equal opportunity policy with a designated complaint officer (Transgender Persons Act ss.9-11); designate an HIV complaints officer at 100+ persons. Code on Wages s.3 bars gender discrimination in pay and recruitment, and forms and interviews must not ask about caste, religion, marital or pregnancy status.
countryAddenda.tw: Employment Services Act Art. 5 bans discrimination on grounds including race, class, language, thought, religion, political party, place of origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, appearance, disability, horoscope and blood type, with fines of NT$300,000-1,500,000. Employers with 67+ employees must employ persons with disabilities equal to at least 1% of headcount or pay the shortfall into the disability employment fund (People with Disabilities Rights Protection Act Art. 38).
countryAddenda.cn: Employment Promotion Law Arts. 26-31 prohibit discrimination by gender, ethnicity, religion, disability, infectious-disease carrier status and rural origin; do not ask women about marriage or childbearing plans, and exclude hepatitis B and pregnancy tests from pre-employment medicals (Women's Rights Law 2022). Local disability employment quotas apply, commonly 1.5% of headcount or a levy (verify Shanghai and Shenzhen rates).

decisions: Keep, rename or restructure DEI programs? (Most US-listed issuers now run open-to-all 'inclusion' programs and keep only locally mandated measures.)
Continue publishing EEO-1 or other workforce demographics voluntarily? (Decide with Legal given the EEO-1 rescission proposal and investor expectations.)
Collect voluntary self-identification outside the US? (Lawful with consent in Canada; limited in China and India; never collect caste.)
Adverse-impact review cadence and privilege structure? (Annual under counsel direction, plus before every RIF.)
Accept federal contracts requiring EO 14173 certifications? (Requires a program inventory and FCA risk assessment first.)
pitfalls: Keeping internships, fellowships or leadership programs restricted by race or sex, now a focus of EEOC, DOJ and FCA enforcement.
10-K or careers-site statements about diversity targets that no longer match actual programs.
Using nationality as a shortcut for export-control risk, creating 1324b and human-rights exposure.
Applying the US protected-class list globally and missing caste, place of origin, horoscope, blood type or hepatitis B carrier status.
Dropping sexual orientation and gender identity from the US policy after the EEOC guidance rescission.
