policies.name: Anti-Harassment
policies.owner: HR (Employee Relations)
policies.approver: CHRO + General Counsel; local entity heads for statutory country instruments (India Internal Committee constitution, Taiwan posted measures)
policies.review: Annual (Ontario and BC require annual program review) + on law change
policies.audience: All employees, interns, contractors, agency workers, visitors, customers and vendors in Company workplaces, at events, on business travel and in virtual channels
policies.purpose: Prohibits harassment, including sexual harassment, on any protected ground and sets how complaints are received, investigated and remedied, using statutory channels where the law requires them. It provides the core Faragher/Ellerth defense in the US and meets mandatory policy contents under California FEHA, Ontario OHSA, BC WorkSafeBC, India's POSH Act, Taiwan's Gender Equality in Employment Act and China's Women's Rights Law.
keyProvisions: Harassment is unwelcome conduct based on a protected characteristic that creates an intimidating, hostile or offensive environment or affects employment decisions; sexual harassment includes quid pro quo, unwelcome advances, requests, comments, jokes, images and physical contact, in person or online (chat, email, video, social media).

The policy covers conduct by and toward employees, interns, contractors, customers, vendors and visitors at work, at Company events, on business travel, at customer and partner sites and in virtual channels.

Complaints may be made to any manager, HR, Ethics & Compliance, the Speak Up hotline or country statutory channels (India Internal Committee, Taiwan GEEA channel, Ontario alternate contact); no one ever has to complain to the person they are complaining about.
Managers who receive or observe potential harassment must notify HR within one business day, even if the complainant asks them not to.

HR acknowledges complaints within 2 business days, decides interim measures (separation, schedule or reporting-line changes, paid leave) that do not disadvantage the complainant, and assigns a trained, impartial investigator.

Investigations aim to conclude within 30 days unless a statutory timetable applies, are documented, and end with written notice of the outcome and any corrective action to both complainant and respondent.
Confidentiality is kept to the extent consistent with a thorough investigation; complainants are never required to agree to confidentiality that prevents them from discussing harassment.
Substantiated harassment results in corrective action up to termination, proportionate to severity; supervisors who engage in quid pro quo harassment are terminated.
Retaliation against complainants, witnesses or anyone who opposes harassment is prohibited.
Everyone completes harassment-prevention training within 6 months of hire and at least every 2 years (annually where local law requires), with a supervisor module at promotion.
The policy is distributed with acknowledgment, posted at each site and translated for any language spoken by 10%+ of a facility's workforce.
Complaint data (volume, type, outcomes, days to close) is reported to the CHRO quarterly and in required local filings such as India's annual POSH report.
policies.sampleLanguage:
Zero Tolerance for Harassment. [Company] prohibits harassment of any kind, including sexual harassment and harassment based on any characteristic protected by law. This applies to everyone who works with us, including employees, interns, contractors, customers and vendors, and it applies wherever work happens: in our offices and labs, at customer and partner sites, at Company events, while traveling and online, including chat, email, video calls and social media.

Sexual harassment includes unwelcome sexual advances, requests for sexual favors, sexual comments or jokes, displaying sexual images, unwelcome touching and any suggestion that a work benefit depends on sexual conduct.

How to Report. You may report harassment to any manager, any member of HR, Ethics & Compliance, the Speak Up hotline or the local committee listed in your country addendum. You never have to report to the person who is harassing you. Managers must promptly notify HR of any harassment they learn about.

Our Response. We will investigate promptly and impartially using trained investigators, take interim steps to protect you, keep information as confidential as possible and tell you the outcome. Anyone found to have harassed others will face discipline up to and including termination. Retaliation against anyone who reports or participates in an investigation is prohibited.

roles.duties: Receives complaints, arranges interim measures, investigates or appoints external investigators and communicates outcomes in writing.
Stop misconduct they observe, notify HR within one business day and implement corrective actions.

roles.role: Statutory committees (India IC; Taiwan investigation committees)
roles.duties: Conduct statutory inquiries and recommend action within legal deadlines.
Advises on privilege, statutory filings and settlement terms, including EFAA, Speak Out Act and CA 12964.5 limits.
Delivers and tracks required training by country and role.
Treat others with respect, report harassment and cooperate in investigations.

countryAddenda.us: Keep sexual orientation and gender identity protections (Bostock; state law) despite the EEOC's Jan 22, 2026 rescission of its harassment guidance. NY requires a written policy and annual interactive training, IL annual training, CT 2 hours within 6 months (3+ employees), DE (50+) within 1 year and every 2 years, ME (15+) within 1 year; under the EFAA sexual-harassment claims cannot be forced into arbitration, and the Speak Out Act makes pre-dispute NDAs unenforceable for such claims.
countryAddenda.us-ca: The policy must meet 2 CCR 11023: list all FEHA categories, allow complaints to someone other than the direct supervisor, and commit to confidentiality, timely and impartial investigation by qualified personnel, documentation, remedial action and non-retaliation, translated for any language spoken by 10%+ of a facility's workforce. Training is 2 hours for supervisors and 1 hour for others within 6 months of hire or promotion and every 2 years, covering abusive conduct, gender identity and expression and sexual orientation (Gov Code 12950.1), with records kept 2 years; settlements must include the Gov Code 12964.5 carve-out.
countryAddenda.ca: Ontario requires a written workplace harassment policy (posted at 6+ workers) and a program developed with the JHSC or representative, covering virtual harassment, an alternate reporting contact, investigation, confidentiality and written results to both parties, reviewed annually (OHSA ss.32.0.6-32.0.8); an inspector can order a third-party investigation at the employer's cost. BC requires a bullying and harassment policy and procedures with a reasonable response aimed at fully addressing the incident, plus training and annual review; any Quebec-based employee triggers a French psychological harassment policy.
countryAddenda.in: Constitute an Internal Committee at each office with 10+ employees (senior woman Presiding Officer, 2+ employee members, one external member, at least half women, 3-year term) and display its details. Complaints are due within 3 months (extendable by 3), the inquiry must finish within 90 days, the report within 10 days and employer action within 60 days, with confidentiality under s.16, an annual report to the District Officer and fines up to INR 50,000; statutory IC jurisdiction covers women complainants, so route other complaints through the global process.
countryAddenda.tw: At 10+ employees set up and publicize a complaint channel; at 30+ adopt and post prevention measures, complaint procedures and disciplinary rules (GEEA Art. 13, amendments in force 8 Mar 2024). Notify the local authority of each complaint and its outcome; complaints against the highest-ranking responsible person may go directly to the authority, and power-based harassment by supervisors carries heavier liability (verify investigation timelines, commonly about 2 months).
countryAddenda.cn: The Women's Rights Law (2022) Art. 25 requires rules, training, a complaint channel, prompt investigation and handling, victim support and anti-retaliation measures, and Civil Code Art. 1010 gives victims a civil claim. Adopt the policy and its disciplinary consequences through democratic procedure with signed acknowledgment so LCL Art. 39 dismissals hold, and keep investigation data in China under PIPL.

decisions: One global case process or separate local processes? (Use one global case system with country steps for India IC inquiries, Taiwan authority notification and Ontario written results.)
When to use external investigators? (VP-and-above respondents, multiple complainants or Board-level matters.)
Training model: one global course plus local modules or fully local courses? (Global core plus CA, NY, IL, Ontario and India POSH modules meets statutory content.)
Extend the India IC process to complaints from men and non-binary employees? (Not statutory; many GCCs do so voluntarily for consistency.)
Allow mutual confidentiality in settlements? (Only within CA 12964.5, Speak Out Act and Rule 21F-17 limits.)
pitfalls: Managers keeping a complaint 'informal' at the complainant's request, destroying the employer's defense.
An India IC without its external member, with expired terms or no annual report, invalidating inquiries.
Ontario investigations that close without written results to both parties.
Relying on a US handbook in China without democratic adoption, so a harassment dismissal is overturned.
Interim measures that disadvantage the complainant, such as moving them off a key project.
policies.training: Harassment-prevention training within 6 months of hire and every 2 years for everyone (California standard applied globally), annual where required (NY, IL, India POSH awareness); supervisor module at promotion; annual training for India IC members.

policies.name: Respectful Workplace & Anti-Bullying
policies.owner: HR (Employee Relations) with EHS for psychological health and safety
policies.approver: CHRO + General Counsel; Taiwan entity representative for posted local measures
policies.review: Annual (BC and Ontario require annual review) + on law change; first Taiwan review six months after the 1 July 2026 go-live
policies.audience: All employees, interns, contractors and agency workers, including conduct toward and from customers, suppliers and visitors
policies.purpose: Prohibits bullying, abusive conduct and psychological harassment that is not tied to a protected ground, and sets prevention, complaint and investigation steps. It meets Taiwan's new workplace-bullying chapter of the OSH Act (in force 1 July 2026), BC's WorkSafeBC bullying and harassment requirements and Ontario's OHSA harassment program, while keeping legitimate performance management clearly outside the definition.
keyProvisions: Bullying is repeated or severe unreasonable conduct, such as humiliation, intimidation, verbal abuse, threats, sabotage of work, exclusion from information needed for the job or excessive monitoring intended to demean, that a reasonable person would know is unwelcome and that harms a worker's dignity or psychological or physical health.
Reasonable management action carried out respectfully (assigning work, setting deadlines, performance feedback, PIPs, discipline, reorganizations) is not bullying.
Complaints may be made through any Speak Up channel or the country bullying channel; anonymous reports are accepted and assessed, though anonymity may limit investigation.

HR acknowledges within 2 business days and, within 5 business days, assesses risk and decides interim protective measures (separation, reporting-line change, paid leave); voluntary mediation is offered only where appropriate and never for severe or power-imbalanced cases.
Investigations are impartial; cases involving senior leaders, or where local law requires, use external investigators or committees with external members.
Outcomes and corrective actions are communicated in writing to the complainant and the respondent.
Leaders are accountable for team climate: engagement-survey items on respect and psychological safety are reviewed with each VP annually.
Overwork is a recognized hazard: managers must not pressure employees to work unrecorded hours or to be continuously available across US-Asia time zones outside agreed on-call schedules.
Retaliation against complainants and witnesses is prohibited.
The policy and procedures are reviewed annually with the joint health and safety committee or worker representatives where one exists.
policies.sampleLanguage:
Respect at Work. Everyone at [Company] deserves to be treated with dignity. We do not tolerate bullying, abusive conduct or psychological harassment, whether it happens in person, in writing, in virtual meetings or on messaging platforms.

Bullying means repeated or serious unreasonable behavior directed at a person or group that a reasonable person would know is unwelcome and that harms their dignity or wellbeing. Examples include shouting or swearing at someone, public humiliation, threats, spreading malicious rumors, deliberately excluding someone from information they need to do their job, and setting impossible tasks to cause failure.

Reasonable actions by managers, such as assigning work, giving honest feedback on performance, managing attendance or taking disciplinary action in a respectful way, are not bullying.

If you experience or witness bullying, report it to your manager, HR, the Speak Up hotline or your local complaint channel. We will respond promptly, take steps to protect you while we look into your concern, investigate impartially and tell you the outcome in writing. We will not tolerate retaliation against anyone who raises a concern in good faith.

roles.duties: Runs the complaint channel, risk assessment, investigations or external investigator appointments, and written outcomes.
Model respectful conduct, address incivility early and escalate complaints within one business day.
Include psychological hazards and overwork in risk assessments and review the policy annually with worker representatives.
Oversees Taiwan case registration and authority referrals and advises on investigation fairness.
Treat colleagues respectfully and report bullying they experience or witness.

countryAddenda.us: No federal or in-scope state statute requires an anti-bullying policy, so apply it as a conduct standard. Under Stericycle (still binding), civility rules must be narrowly tailored with a Section 7 savings clause so employees can criticize management or working conditions.
countryAddenda.us-ca: Gov Code 12950.1 requires harassment training to cover prevention of 'abusive conduct' (malicious conduct a reasonable person would find hostile and offensive, unrelated to legitimate business interests), so use this policy's definitions in California training. Workplace violence restraining orders may now also be sought for harassment (CCP 527.8).
countryAddenda.ca: Ontario's OHSA definition of workplace harassment includes vexatious comment or conduct that is not tied to a protected ground, so this policy forms part of the OHSA harassment program with alternate reporting, investigation and written results. BC requires a bullying and harassment policy, reporting and investigation procedures with a reasonable response, training of workers and supervisors and annual review (WorkSafeBC policies; verify policy numbers).
countryAddenda.in: No statute addresses bullying; incorporate the policy into service rules or standing orders so misconduct can be disciplined after a domestic enquiry, and let workers use the Grievance Redressal Committee (20+ workers; 30-day resolution).
countryAddenda.tw: From 1 July 2026 the OSH Act bullying chapter requires a publicized complaint channel at 10+ employees and, at 30+, adopted and disclosed prevention measures, complaint and investigation procedures and disciplinary rules; register each case in MOL's reporting system and refer complaints against the top responsible person to the local authority. Investigation committees need at least half external members where the rules require, and fines run NT$30,000-750,000 for employer failures and up to NT$1M for a top executive who bullies.
countryAddenda.cn: No specific bullying statute exists; list bullying as a defined violation in the democratically adopted handbook and handle complaints through HR, involving the union where one exists. Keep investigation data in China under PIPL.

decisions: One combined respectful-workplace and anti-harassment policy, or separate policies? (Separate policies help Taiwan and BC compliance; a combined policy is simpler for employees.)
Offer mediation as a first step? (Useful for low-level conflict; never for severe or power-imbalanced cases.)
Threshold for external investigators (VP+ respondents, multiple complainants)? (Taiwan rules may require external committee members.)
Cover conduct at customer sites and by customers (e.g., FAEs at customer fabs)? (Taiwan's rules reach client sites; recommended globally.)
Use engagement-survey respect items as a leadership KPI? (Improves accountability; keep anonymity thresholds.)
pitfalls: Treating legitimate PIPs as bullying, or dismissing bullying as 'performance management', because definitions are vague.
Missing Taiwan's July 2026 requirements: MOL case registration and authority referral of complaints against the top executive.
Not reviewing BC and Ontario programs annually, a common inspection finding.
Broad 'be positive' civility rules that chill NLRA-protected speech in the US.
policies.training: Respectful-workplace module at hire and every 2 years; supervisor module at promotion; annual information to Taiwan and BC workers on complaint procedures.

policies.name: Workplace Violence Prevention
policies.owner: Security (Corporate Security) with EHS; Employee Relations for employee-related threat assessment
policies.approver: Chief Security Officer + CHRO + General Counsel; site leads approve site-specific plans
policies.review: Annual plan review (required in California and Ontario) and after every serious incident
policies.audience: All employees, contractors, visitors and customers at Company sites, labs and events and during business travel; remote workers for threats received
policies.purpose: Prevents and responds to violence, threats and intimidation through site-specific plans, threat assessment and incident response. It satisfies California's Workplace Violence Prevention Plan requirement (Labor Code 6401.9, SB 553), Ontario's OHSA violence program and Taiwan's unlawful-infringement prevention duty, and links violence prevention to lab access, insider-threat and RIF security.
keyProvisions: Prohibited: physical violence, threats (direct, veiled or online), intimidation, stalking, harassment with violent intent, and weapons on Company premises or at Company events except where the law requires otherwise.

Each site keeps a written, site-specific workplace violence prevention plan developed with employee and representative involvement, naming responsible persons and covering hazards (reception and public access, lab and cleanroom access, night and weekend work, parking), controls, reporting and emergency response.

Anyone facing an immediate threat calls emergency services, then Security; all other threats or concerning behavior are reported to Security or HR the same day, and no one is retaliated against for reporting or seeking emergency help.

A Threat Assessment Team (Security, Employee Relations, Legal, EHS and a clinical advisor as needed) convenes within 24 hours of a credible threat and decides interim measures such as paid administrative leave, access suspension, no-contact directives or protective orders.
Every incident is recorded in a violent incident log (date, location, type, roles of the people involved without names, consequences and corrective actions) and investigated to correct hazards.
Employees receive interactive training on the plan at hire and annually: how to report, warning signs, de-escalation and emergency procedures.
High-risk separations (terminations with threat indicators, RIFs) require a security plan covering access-revocation timing, meeting location, escort and post-exit monitoring.
Domestic or intimate-partner violence that may reach the workplace is handled confidentially with a safety plan and leave or accommodation where available.
Remote employees report threats received online; Security coordinates with local law enforcement as needed.
Hazard, incident and investigation records are kept at least 5 years and training records at least 1 year, or longer where local law requires.
policies.sampleLanguage:
Our Commitment. [Company] is committed to a workplace free from violence, threats and intimidation. This policy applies to everyone at our offices, labs and other sites, at customer and partner facilities, at Company events and during business travel.

Prohibited Conduct. You may not engage in or threaten physical violence, make threatening statements or gestures, intimidate, stalk or harass others, damage property to intimidate anyone, or bring weapons onto Company property except where the law expressly permits it.

Reporting. If you face an immediate threat, call emergency services first, then contact Security at [number]. Report any other threat, violent act or concerning behavior to Security, HR or the Speak Up hotline as soon as possible. You may also ask for help if you are experiencing domestic violence that could affect your safety at work; we will handle your request confidentially.

Our Response. Every report is reviewed by our Threat Assessment Team, which may take protective steps such as restricting access, issuing no-contact directions or seeking a restraining order. Each site's Workplace Violence Prevention Plan describes local procedures and responsible persons. We will not retaliate against anyone who reports in good faith or seeks help during an emergency.

roles.duties: Owns site plans, access control, the Threat Assessment Team and law-enforcement liaison.
Integrates violence hazards into the IIPP and OHS programs, runs annual reviews with committees and maintains incident logs.
Assesses employee-related threats and manages administrative leave and corrective action.
Report concerning behavior immediately and follow the security plan for high-risk separations.
Complete training, report threats and follow emergency procedures.

countryAddenda.us: There is no federal workplace violence standard, but the OSH Act General Duty Clause applies and serious injuries must be recorded and reported (fatalities within 8 hours; inpatient hospitalizations within 24 hours). Check state firearms-in-parking-lot laws for any US sites outside California (verify) and state protective-order procedures.
countryAddenda.us-ca: Each covered California site needs a written WVPP under Labor Code 6401.9 (SB 553): employee involvement, annual interactive training, a violent incident log, post-incident investigation, annual review, employee access to records within 15 days, and records kept 5 years (training 1 year); exemptions cover sites closed to the public with fewer than 10 employees and remote workers. Employers may seek restraining orders for violence and harassment (CCP 527.8), employees may leave during emergency conditions without retaliation (LC 1139), and Cal/OSHA must adopt a general-industry standard by 31 Dec 2026.
countryAddenda.ca: Ontario requires a written workplace violence policy (posted at 6+ workers), a risk assessment, and a program with measures for summoning immediate help, reporting and investigation, reviewed annually, plus every reasonable precaution where domestic violence may occur in the workplace (OHSA ss.32.0.1-32.0.5). BC requires a violence risk assessment with procedures and training (OHS Regulation Part 4; verify sections).
countryAddenda.in: No specific statute; apply the OSH Code general duty, and for night shifts obtain women's written consent and provide safe transport and security (OSH Code s.43; Karnataka Shops Act s.25). Bengaluru sites should keep cab safety measures (GPS, escort) despite the 2026 Karnataka deregulation.
countryAddenda.tw: OSH Act Art. 6(2) requires planning and measures to prevent physical or verbal unlawful infringement during work; sites with 100+ workers need a written plan with implementation records, and smaller sites keep execution records. Coordinate with the workplace-bullying chapter in force from 1 July 2026 where conduct overlaps.
countryAddenda.cn: Apply the Work Safety Law responsibility system (a safety function or full-time safety staff above 100 employees) and involve public security authorities for violence. Threat-assessment information is personal information under PIPL, so collect only what is necessary and keep it in China.

decisions: Standalone WVPP per site or integrated into the IIPP/OHS program? (California allows either; standalone plans make annual review simpler.)
Weapons rule: total ban, or storage in locked vehicles where state law protects it? (Depends on US sites outside California.)
Paid administrative leave as the default during threat assessment? (Reduces risk; document it as non-disciplinary.)
Retain a behavioral threat-assessment vendor or clinician? (Recommended at 1,500+ employees.)
Link insider-threat and workplace-violence programs? (Useful for RIFs and departing engineers; requires privacy review.)
pitfalls: One generic corporate WVPP that is not tailored to each California site or developed without employee involvement.
Violent incident logs that include names or are not kept for 5 years.
Terminating an employee who has made threats without a security plan or coordinated access revocation.
Ignoring domestic-violence risks that follow employees to work.
policies.training: Interactive WVPP training at hire and annually at every site with a plan (California requirement applied globally); Ontario violence program information at hire; annual Threat Assessment Team training.

policies.name: Drug, Alcohol & Substance Use
policies.owner: HR (Employee Relations) with EHS
policies.approver: CHRO + General Counsel
policies.review: Every 2 years + on law change (cannabis and testing laws change frequently)
policies.audience: All employees, interns and contractors while working, on Company premises (including labs), driving on Company business or attending Company events
policies.purpose: Keeps workplaces safe from impairment, especially validation, reliability and failure-analysis labs with chemicals, lasers, X-ray and high-voltage equipment, while respecting off-duty cannabis protections, the duty to accommodate addiction as a disability, and privacy limits on testing. It defines fitness-for-duty expectations, narrow testing triggers and support options.
keyProvisions: Employees must be fit for duty and may not work while impaired by alcohol, cannabis, illegal drugs or misused medication.

Possessing, using, selling or distributing illegal drugs on Company premises or while working is prohibited; alcohol may be served only at Company events approved by a VP with responsible-service controls, and never in labs.

Employees in safety-sensitive roles (hazardous chemicals, lasers, X-ray, high-voltage benches, powered equipment, driving on Company business) must tell EHS about any medication that may impair safe work, without disclosing the diagnosis.

Testing is limited to: reasonable suspicion based on documented, observed signs of impairment (confirmed by two trained observers where practicable); post-incident testing where impairment could plausibly have contributed, never as automatic retaliation for reporting an injury; and testing required by law or customer contract. Random testing is used only where lawful for designated safety-sensitive roles.
Test methods measure current impairment where possible (breath alcohol, oral fluid) and do not rely on non-psychoactive cannabis metabolites.
An employee suspected of impairment is removed from work, not allowed to drive and sent home safely at Company expense pending review.

Employees who disclose a substance-use disorder before a violation are offered support (EAP, leave, treatment accommodation) under the Reasonable Accommodation policy; disclosure after a violation does not excuse misconduct but is considered.
Test results and medical information are confidential, stored separately from personnel files and shared only on a need-to-know basis.
Lawful off-duty cannabis use is not a basis for adverse action where protected by law, except for roles the law exempts (e.g., federal security clearance).
Violations result in corrective action up to termination, following local procedure.
policies.sampleLanguage:
Fitness for Duty. Every employee is responsible for arriving at work, and remaining throughout the working day, fit to perform their job safely. You may not work, operate lab equipment, handle hazardous materials or drive on Company business while impaired by alcohol, cannabis, illegal drugs or medication. If you take a prescribed or over-the-counter medication that may affect your ability to work safely in a lab or other safety-sensitive role, tell EHS so that we can adjust your duties; you do not need to disclose your diagnosis.

Prohibited Conduct. Using, possessing, selling or distributing illegal drugs on Company premises or while working is prohibited. Alcohol may be served only at approved Company events, and you are expected to drink responsibly.

Reasonable Suspicion. If a manager observes signs that you may be impaired, you will be removed from work and safely transported home, and you may be asked to take a test where permitted by local law.

Getting Help. [Company] supports employees who seek help for alcohol or drug dependency. Confidential support is available through our Employee Assistance Program, and you may request leave or other accommodation for treatment.

roles.duties: Recognize and document signs of impairment, remove the employee from work safely and contact HR immediately.
Decides on testing within legal limits and manages corrective action and accommodation.
Designates safety-sensitive roles, handles medication notifications and builds impairment risk into lab safety rules.
Confirms that testing is lawful in each jurisdiction and reviews post-incident testing practice.
Report fit for duty, notify EHS of impairing medication in safety-sensitive roles and seek help early.

countryAddenda.us: Carve out state-protected off-duty cannabis use (e.g., NY, NJ, MN; WA pre-hire) except for safety-sensitive or federally regulated roles; current illegal drug users are not protected by the ADA, but people in recovery are. Post-incident testing must not deter injury reporting (29 CFR 1904.35(b)(1)(iv)), and covered federal contracts or grants require a Drug-Free Workplace Act statement and awareness program.
countryAddenda.us-ca: Gov Code 12954 (AB 2188, SB 700) bars discrimination for off-duty, off-premises cannabis use or non-psychoactive metabolite results and bars asking applicants about past cannabis use, except for roles requiring federal background investigations or security clearances and federally mandated testing. Random testing is limited by the constitutional privacy right to safety-sensitive roles, reasonable-suspicion testing needs documented impairment signs, and employers with 25+ employees must reasonably accommodate voluntary rehabilitation (Labor Code 1025).
countryAddenda.ca: Addiction is a disability under the Ontario and BC Human Rights Codes, so the duty to accommodate to undue hardship applies, and random testing is generally not permitted outside dangerous workplaces with evidence of a problem (Irving Pulp & Paper, 2013 SCC 34). Recreational cannabis is legal, so treat it like alcohol: impairment at work is the issue, and a positive test alone rarely justifies termination.
countryAddenda.in: No statute governs workplace testing; testing needs informed consent and results are sensitive personal data under the SPDI Rules (DPDP from 13 May 2027). Define intoxication and possession as misconduct in service rules or standing orders so discipline can follow a domestic enquiry.
countryAddenda.tw: List impairment and drug-related misconduct in the filed work rules; testing requires notice and written consent because results are sensitive health data under PDPA Art. 6. Illegal drug use and possession are also offenses under the Narcotics Hazard Prevention Act (verify categories).
countryAddenda.cn: List intoxication at work and drug-related misconduct as serious violations in the democratically adopted handbook; an employee held criminally liable may be dismissed (LCL Art. 39(6)), while dismissal after administrative detention for drug use depends on handbook terms (verify). Testing data is sensitive PI requiring separate consent under PIPL.

decisions: Pre-employment drug testing: none, safety-sensitive roles only, or all US hires? (Most fabless companies test none or only safety-sensitive roles; California limits testing.)
Which roles are safety-sensitive? (Lab technicians, FA and reliability engineers using chemicals or lasers, drivers.)
Alcohol at Company events and customer entertainment in Asia? (Allow with limits, non-alcoholic options and safe transport; never at lab sites.)
Use last-chance agreements after treatment? (Common in Canada; review for human rights compliance.)
Test method: oral fluid or urine? (Oral fluid better reflects current impairment.)
pitfalls: Rejecting California candidates for cannabis metabolites or asking about past use.
Automatic post-injury testing that discourages injury reporting.
Terminating a Canadian employee for a positive test without exploring accommodation of addiction.
Testing in China or Taiwan without separate written consent for sensitive data.
policies.training: Acknowledgment at hire; lab safety induction covers fitness for duty; reasonable-suspicion training for managers of safety-sensitive teams every 2 years.

policies.name: Standards of Conduct & Corrective Action
policies.owner: HR (Employee Relations)
policies.approver: CHRO + General Counsel; local adoption as required (China democratic procedure, Taiwan work-rule filing, India standing orders or service rules)
policies.review: Every 2 years + on law change
policies.audience: All employees and interns; contractors through their agencies
policies.purpose: Defines expected workplace conduct, categories of misconduct and the corrective-action options, and sets a fair, documented and locally lawful disciplinary process. It keeps discipline consistent across countries while meeting the procedural rules that make it enforceable: just cause in Canada, domestic enquiry in India, filed work rules in Taiwan and democratically adopted rules in China.
keyProvisions: Employees must follow the Code, Company policies, lawful instructions, safety and security rules (including lab, Technology Control Plan and export-control access rules) and attendance and timekeeping requirements.

Misconduct is classified as minor (e.g., lateness, minor policy lapses), serious (e.g., insubordination, repeated violations, careless data handling) or gross (e.g., theft, fraud, violence, harassment, falsifying records including timecards, expense reports or test data, deliberate export-control or TCP breaches, exfiltration of confidential information).

Corrective-action options are coaching, documented verbal warning, written warning, final written warning, suspension (paid pending investigation; unpaid only where lawful and contractually permitted) and termination; steps may be skipped for serious or gross misconduct.
Before any written warning or more serious action, the employee is told the allegation and given an opportunity to respond, and the facts are investigated proportionately.
Performance shortfalls (as opposed to misconduct) are handled under the Performance Management policy, including a PIP where appropriate.
Every action beyond coaching is documented in Darwinbox with the facts, policy reference, employee response and decision-maker; Employee Relations checks consistency with prior cases.
HR and Legal review every proposed termination for recent protected activity (complaints, leave, accommodation requests, whistleblowing in the prior 12 months) and for local procedural requirements.
Warnings remain active for 12 months (final written warnings 24 months) for escalation purposes unless local rules differ.
Fines and wage deductions are never used as discipline.
Nothing in this policy changes at-will employment in the US; outside the US, employment ends only in accordance with local law and the employment contract.
policies.sampleLanguage:
Standards of Conduct. [Company] expects every employee to act honestly, treat others with respect, follow Company policies and safety rules, and protect the Company's confidential information and technology. Examples of serious misconduct that may lead to immediate termination include theft or fraud; falsifying records, including timesheets, expense reports or test data; violence or threats; harassment; unauthorized access to, copying or transfer of confidential information or controlled technology; and deliberate violation of export-control or security procedures.

Corrective Action. When conduct falls short of our standards, [Company] will respond in a way that is fair and proportionate. Depending on the seriousness of the conduct and the employee's record, corrective action may include coaching, a verbal or written warning, a final written warning, suspension or termination. [Company] may begin at any step when the circumstances warrant.

Fair Process. Before taking formal corrective action, we will explain the concern to you and give you an opportunity to respond. Corrective action will be documented, and you will receive a copy of any written warning.

Local Requirements. Where local law or approved work rules prescribe a specific procedure, that procedure will be followed.

roles.duties: Address conduct early, gather facts, consult HR before formal action and deliver corrective action respectfully.
Investigates, ensures fair process and consistency, documents actions and applies local procedures.
Reviews terminations for legal risk and local procedural compliance.
Receives legally required notifications, such as China's union notice before a unilateral termination.
Follow the standards, respond honestly to allegations and may seek review through the grievance process.

countryAddenda.us: Preserve at-will language and keep conduct rules NLRA-compliant (Stericycle savings clause). Document legitimate reasons for all adverse actions, including transfers and job changes (Muldrow v. St. Louis, 2024), and check timing against any protected activity.
countryAddenda.us-ca: Adverse action within 90 days of protected wage, whistleblower or equal-pay activity is presumed retaliatory (Labor Code 98.6, 1102.5; SB 497), so require Legal review; final pay is due immediately on discharge (LC 201-203). Unpaid disciplinary suspensions of exempt employees must meet FLSA and state salary-basis rules.
countryAddenda.ca: There is no at-will employment: proportionate, progressive discipline is usually needed to establish just cause (McKinley v. BC Tel), and Ontario ESA notice and severance are forfeited only for 'wilful misconduct, disobedience or wilful neglect of duty'. Unpaid suspensions without a contractual right can be constructive dismissal (Potter, 2015 SCC 10).
countryAddenda.in: Misconduct dismissal of 'workers' requires a domestic enquiry: charge sheet, reply, impartial enquiry officer, hearing with evidence and cross-examination, report, second show-cause on penalty and a reasoned order, with subsistence allowance during suspension as the standing orders provide. IT/ITeS establishments relying on the Karnataka standing-orders exemption must report suspensions, discharges and dismissals to the Deputy Labour Commissioner.
countryAddenda.tw: Only conduct listed in the filed work rules (30+ employees) can be disciplined, and a serious-misconduct dismissal must fit an LSA Art. 12 ground and be carried out within 30 days of learning of it. LSA Art. 26 prohibits deducting penalties from wages, so do not use fines.
countryAddenda.cn: Disciplinary rules are enforceable only if adopted through democratic procedure and acknowledged (LCL Art. 4); define 'serious violations' concretely to support Art. 39 dismissal and notify the union before any unilateral termination (Art. 43). Deductions for employee-caused losses are capped at 20% of monthly wage and may not reduce pay below minimum wage.

decisions: Progressive discipline as a mandatory process or a guideline? (A guideline in the US to preserve at-will; effectively mandatory in Canada, India, Taiwan and China.)
Warning validity periods: 12 or 24 months?
Termination approval: HRBP + VP, or Employee Relations + Legal? (ER + Legal for protected-activity and all non-US cases.)
Adopt a global misconduct matrix? (Improves consistency and local enforceability; keep discretion language.)
Suspension pending investigation: paid or unpaid? (Paid by default to avoid constructive-dismissal and wage claims.)
pitfalls: Relying on a US handbook to dismiss in China or Taiwan without local adoption or filing.
Inconsistent discipline for similar misconduct across countries or demographic groups.
Skipping the employee's chance to respond, undermining just cause and natural justice.
Using fines or wage deductions as discipline, which breaches Taiwan, China and California wage laws.
Missing Taiwan's 30-day window for LSA Art. 12 dismissals.
policies.training: Acknowledgment at hire and on material change; manager training on fair process and documentation at promotion.

policies.name: Social Media & External Communications
policies.owner: Corporate Communications with Legal (Securities) and HR
policies.approver: General Counsel + Chief Communications Officer + CHRO
policies.review: Annual
policies.audience: All employees, interns and contractors; enhanced rules for executives, IR, sales, FAEs and engineers with customer, roadmap or tape-out information
policies.purpose: Protects material nonpublic and customer-confidential information and makes sure only authorized spokespeople speak for the Company, consistent with Regulation FD, customer NDAs and export-control rules. It also preserves employees' legal rights to discuss working conditions (NLRA Section 7) and to communicate with regulators.
keyProvisions: Only authorized spokespeople (CEO, CFO, IR, Corporate Communications and named designees) may speak for the Company to media, analysts, investors or the public; all such inquiries go to Corporate Communications or IR.

Employees must not disclose MNPI on any channel, including unannounced financial results, design wins, customer names or ramps, tape-out and qualification status, product roadmaps, export-license outcomes, M&A or RIFs.

Customer and partner confidential information, including customer names protected by NDA, may not be disclosed, and no photos may be posted from labs or showing whiteboards, wafers, boards or screens.

Technical papers, conference talks and open-source contributions require pre-approval from the manager and Legal/IP, and from Trade Compliance where technology may be export-controlled (to confirm it qualifies as published before release).
Employees who identify their employer when posting about the industry must state that views are their own; no one may post on behalf of the Company without authorization.
Recruiting and employer-brand content is reviewed by Communications and may not reveal customers, roadmaps or headcount plans.
Harassing, threatening or discriminatory posts about colleagues, customers or partners are prohibited.
Any accidental disclosure of possible MNPI must be reported to Legal immediately so the Company can make public disclosure within Regulation FD timelines.
Nothing in this policy restricts employees from discussing wages, hours or working conditions, engaging in protected concerted activity or communicating with government agencies.
Company social media accounts belong to the Company; credentials are held by Communications and returned at exit.
policies.sampleLanguage:
Speaking for [Company]. Only employees authorized by Corporate Communications or Investor Relations may speak on behalf of [Company] to journalists, analysts, investors or the public. If you are contacted by the media or an investor, do not comment; refer the inquiry to [email].

Protecting Confidential Information. Never share material nonpublic information about [Company], or confidential information about our customers, suppliers or partners, on social media or in any other public forum. This includes unannounced financial results, customer wins or losses, product roadmaps, tape-out or qualification results and pending transactions. Do not post photos taken in labs or showing screens, whiteboards, boards or wafers. Technical papers, conference presentations and open-source contributions must be approved in advance.

Personal Social Media. When you discuss our industry online and identify yourself as a [Company] employee, make clear that your views are your own. Treat colleagues, customers and competitors with respect.

Your Rights. This policy does not restrict your right to discuss your wages, hours or other terms and conditions of employment with coworkers or others, to engage in other legally protected activity, or to communicate with any government agency.

roles.duties: Authorizes spokespeople, reviews employer-brand and technical content and manages Company accounts.
Assesses possible MNPI disclosures and Regulation FD remediation and approves publication of sensitive information.
Confirms the export-control status of technical publications and talks before release.
Approve technical publications and remind teams of confidentiality around customer events and launches.
Refer inquiries, protect MNPI and customer information and follow pre-approval rules.

countryAddenda.us: Regulation FD requires simultaneous (intentional) or prompt (within 24 hours or before the next market open) public disclosure when MNPI is selectively disclosed to market professionals or holders. Stericycle remains binding despite the NLRB's new Republican majority, so keep rules narrowly tailored with a Section 7 savings clause and never require approval to discuss working conditions.
countryAddenda.us-ca: Labor Code 980 bars requesting personal social media passwords or access (narrow exception for investigating misconduct), Labor Code 1101-1102 protect political activity and 96(k)/98.6 protect lawful off-duty conduct, so tailor discipline for off-duty posts accordingly.
countryAddenda.ca: Discipline for off-duty posts requires a real connection to the employer's interests (reputation, harassment of colleagues, confidentiality); disclose any monitoring of public posts in the Ontario electronic monitoring policy and under BC PIPA. Provide a French version for any Quebec-based employee.
countryAddenda.in: Posts identifying colleagues or customers can raise defamation and IT Act issues; disclose monitoring of Company systems under the SPDI Rules and, from 13 May 2027, DPDP notice rules. Incorporate the policy into service rules so breaches can be disciplined.
countryAddenda.tw: Incorporate the policy into the filed work rules; any monitoring of employees' public posts must be proportionate and disclosed in the PDPA notice. Remind engineers that posts touching national core key technologies or government projects create National Security Act and Trade Secrets Act exposure.
countryAddenda.cn: Posts on WeChat, Weibo or Maimai about the Company, customers or US-China trade issues can create Cybersecurity Law, Data Security Law ('important data') and Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law exposure, so employees must not comment publicly on export-control matters. Adopt through democratic procedure so violations can be disciplined.

decisions: Run an employee advocacy program (sharing approved posts)? (Helps recruiting; needs disclosure rules and Regulation FD review of content.)
Pre-approval scope: all external technical talks or only those on unreleased products?
Monitor public social media: brand-level only or employee-specific? (Brand-level only is safer under the NLRA and privacy laws.)
Allow employees to name customers in LinkedIn profiles? (Usually no for NDA customers.)
Designate local spokespeople in Asia for regional media?
pitfalls: Engineers posting 'excited to announce we taped out for [customer]' before public announcement, creating MNPI and NDA breaches.
Broad bans on 'disparaging' posts or approval requirements for discussing work conditions, violating NLRA Section 7.
Conference presentations given without export-control review of technical content.
Recruiting posts that reveal headcount plans for a new product line or an upcoming RIF.
policies.training: Acknowledgment at hire; annual MNPI and confidentiality training for engineers, FAEs, sales and IR; media training for authorized spokespeople.

policies.name: Human Rights & Labor Standards
policies.owner: Ethics & Compliance / ESG with HR (own operations) and Procurement (supply chain)
policies.approver: CEO + CHRO + General Counsel; Nominating & Governance Committee oversight
policies.review: Annual; aligned with RBA Code updates and customer audit cycles
policies.audience: All Company operations and employees; contractors, agency and dispatch workers, labor agents and suppliers through the Supplier Code
policies.purpose: Commits the Company to respect internationally recognized human rights and the Responsible Business Alliance (RBA) Code of Conduct v8.0, which semiconductor customers require of their suppliers, in its own operations and supply chain. It sets concrete labor standards on freely chosen employment, recruitment fees, working hours, wages, young workers, humane treatment, non-discrimination and freedom of association, with due diligence and remediation.
keyProvisions: The Company prohibits forced, bonded, indentured, trafficked and prison labor; workers are free to resign on legally required notice and to leave Company premises.
Workers never pay recruitment fees or related costs (agency, visa, medical, travel) to obtain employment; any fees discovered are repaid by the Company or the responsible agent within 90 days.
The Company and its agents never hold workers' passports, identity documents, original certificates or work permits beyond brief verification.
Workers receive written terms of employment in a language they understand before starting, and before departure for migrant workers.

No child labor: the minimum hiring age is the higher of 16 or the local legal minimum, age is verified at hire, and workers under 18 do no hazardous lab work, night work or overtime; student interns work under internship agreements and never fill regular roles.

Working hours, including overtime, may not exceed the lower of local legal limits or 60 hours per week except in genuine emergencies; workers receive at least one day off in seven; overtime is voluntary and paid at legal premium rates.
Wages meet or exceed legal minimums, are paid on time with clear pay statements, and are never reduced as a disciplinary measure.
Workers may join or not join lawful worker organizations and bargain collectively where lawful, without retaliation.
Grievance channels (Speak Up hotline, local committees) are open to contractors, agency workers and supplier workers, with anonymity where lawful and non-retaliation.

Ethics & Compliance runs a human-rights risk assessment of own sites and high-risk suppliers (labor agents, dispatch agencies, OSAT and foundry partners, facility services) every two years and tracks remediation to closure.
Labor agents, staffing and dispatch agencies are screened against restricted-party and UFLPA lists and must contractually comply with this policy and permit audits.
The Company maps this policy to RBA Code clauses for customer SAQs and VAP audits and publishes an annual summary of due-diligence results.
policies.sampleLanguage:
Our Commitment. [Company] respects the human rights of everyone who works for us or on our behalf. We align our standards with the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, the ILO Declaration on Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work, the OECD Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises and the Responsible Business Alliance Code of Conduct, and we expect our suppliers and labor agents to do the same.

Freely Chosen Employment. We do not use forced, bonded, trafficked or prison labor. No worker will be required to pay a fee to obtain a job with us or with any agency supplying workers to us; if we find that a worker has paid such a fee, we will make sure it is repaid. We do not hold workers' identity documents.

Working Hours and Wages. Working hours will not exceed local legal limits or 60 hours per week, including overtime, except in emergencies, and workers will have at least one day off every seven days. All overtime is voluntary and paid at legally required rates.

Voice and Remedy. Workers may raise concerns through our Speak Up channels without fear of retaliation, and we will work to remedy any adverse impact we cause or contribute to.

roles.duties: Owns the policy, human-rights risk assessments, RBA SAQs and remediation tracking.
Applies the standards in own operations: hours monitoring, age verification, contracts and grievance handling.
Flows requirements down to labor agents and suppliers and screens and audits them.
Advises on forced-labor import rules, Canadian supply-chain reporting and remediation.
Plan workloads within hours limits and never pressure workers to give up rest days or overtime pay.

countryAddenda.us: Goods made wholly or partly in Xinjiang or by UFLPA Entity List companies are presumed made with forced labor and barred from import, so confirm HR vendors and labor agents are not listed. Track hours for non-exempt lab and support staff under the FLSA, and capture exempt engineers' hours during tape-out crunches so the RBA 60-hour limit can be evidenced.
countryAddenda.us-ca: Track daily overtime (over 8 hours a day) and 7th-day rules for non-exempt lab technicians to evidence RBA hours compliance, and confirm labor contractors meet wage-and-hour obligations; employers using 100+ workers through labor contractors file a separate CRD pay data report.
countryAddenda.ca: Confirm whether the Canadian subsidiary meets the Fighting Against Forced Labour and Child Labour in Supply Chains Act size tests (commonly two of C$20M assets, C$40M revenue, 250 employees; verify) and, if so, supply HR inputs for the report due by May 31 each year. Ontario and BC hours rules (ON overtime after 44 hours a week; BC after 8 hours a day or 40 a week) set local limits.
countryAddenda.in: Karnataka now bans employers from keeping employees' original certificates (2026 amendment), so verify and return them the same day. Workers' overtime is capped (144 hours a quarter under the central rules; 50 under the Karnataka 24x7 notification) and paid at double rate, and contract-labour agencies must be licensed and audited (verify OSH Code thresholds).
countryAddenda.tw: Employment Services Act Art. 5 bans withholding ID documents; overtime is capped at 46 hours a month (54 a month and 138 per 3 months with labor-management meeting consent) with 11 hours between shifts. Audit facility-service contractors that employ migrant workers for broker-fee practices (verify applicable caps).
countryAddenda.cn: Standard hours are 8 a day and 40 a week with overtime normally capped at 36 hours a month, and dispatched workers may fill only temporary, auxiliary or substitute roles up to 10% of the workforce with equal pay. Route any conflict between US forced-labor due diligence and PRC counter-sanctions law through Legal.

decisions: Apply the RBA 60-hour limit globally or only the stricter local limit? (The RBA expects the lower of the two.)
Join the RBA or only follow the Code for customers? (Membership brings VAP commitments and supply-chain cascade duties.)
Scope of employer-pays: direct hires only, or all agency, dispatch and supplier workers? (The RBA expects all.)
Approval level for the human rights policy: CEO or a Board committee? (The UNGPs expect the most senior level.)
Publish a standalone human rights report or fold it into the sustainability report?
pitfalls: Ignoring agency and facility-service workers (cleaning, security, canteen) whose recruitment fees become audit findings.
No hours data for exempt engineers during tape-out crunches, so RBA hours compliance cannot be shown.
Keeping original degree certificates in India or passports for visa processing longer than necessary.
Customer-facing policy statements that do not match practices audited in VAP.
policies.training: Acknowledgment at hire; annual training for HR, Procurement and Asia site leaders on forced-labor indicators and migrant-worker protections; RBA audit-readiness briefing before each VAP audit.

policies.name: Recruitment & Selection
policies.owner: Talent Acquisition (Head of TA)
policies.approver: CHRO + General Counsel
policies.review: Annual + on law change (pay-transparency and AI-in-hiring rules change frequently)
policies.audience: All hiring managers, interviewers, recruiters, TA coordinators and agencies; all candidates for employee and intern roles worldwide
policies.purpose: Sets how the Company attracts and selects talent fairly, lawfully and consistently: approved requisitions, compliant postings with pay ranges, structured interviews, documented decisions and controlled offers. It builds in the location-specific rules on pay transparency, salary-history bans, AI disclosure and candidate privacy, and the chip-industry controls on export screening, prior-employer IP and anti-corruption.
keyProvisions: No position may be posted or filled without an approved requisition in Darwinbox/Greenhouse tied to the workforce plan and job architecture (job code, level, pay range, export-control flag, location, sponsorship eligibility).

Every posting that may be filled in a pay-transparency jurisdiction shows a good-faith pay range (and a benefits summary where required); all US postings show a range, Ontario ranges may not exceed a C$50,000 spread, and BC postings always show pay.
Recruiters and interviewers must not ask about or rely on salary history; they may ask about pay expectations.

Each role uses a structured interview plan with defined competencies, standard questions and a scorecard; each interviewer submits independent feedback in Greenhouse within 1 business day and before the debrief.
Professional roles are assessed by at least 3 trained interviewers, and no offer is made without a documented debrief decision.

Any AI or automated tool used to source, screen, assess or rank candidates must be approved by Legal and HR Analytics after bias testing, disclosed to candidates where required, and subject to human review of adverse outcomes.

Questions must be job-related; questions about protected characteristics, family plans, medical history (before an offer), criminal history (where restricted before an offer) and citizenship (other than the approved export-control question for flagged roles) are prohibited.

Candidates confirm they will not bring or use any prior employer's confidential information; interviewers may not solicit or accept code, design files or technical details belonging to a former employer.

Offers follow the offer-approval workflow: in-range offers are approved by the hiring manager and HRBP; offers above the 75th percentile of range, sign-on bonuses and above-guideline equity need Total Rewards and VP approval.
Candidates related to employees, government officials or customer personnel are routed under the Workplace Relationships and Anti-Bribery policies before an offer.
Agencies are used only under a signed Company agreement, and unsolicited CVs create no fee obligation.
policies.sampleLanguage:
Fair and Consistent Hiring. [Company] selects candidates based on their ability to perform the job. Every opening must be supported by an approved requisition and posted with a job description that reflects the essential duties and qualifications. Where required by law, and for all positions in the United States, postings will include a good-faith pay range.

Structured Selection. Hiring teams must use the structured interview plan for the role, ask job-related questions and record independent written feedback before discussing candidates. Interviewers may not ask candidates about their salary history, age, family plans, religion, health or other protected characteristics. If a role requires access to export-controlled technology, the recruiter will ask the approved export-control question; no other questions about citizenship or immigration status may be asked.

Technology in Hiring. Automated tools may support, but not replace, human judgment, and may be used only if approved by HR and Legal. Candidates will be told when such tools are used where the law requires.

Protecting Others' Information. We respect the intellectual property of other companies. Candidates must not share, and interviewers must not request, confidential information belonging to a current or former employer.

roles.duties: Opens compliant postings, screens against approved criteria, coordinates structured interviews and manages offers.
Defines job-related requirements, leads the debrief and makes documented, merit-based decisions.
Complete training, assess assigned competencies and submit independent feedback within 1 business day.
Sets pay ranges and approves out-of-guideline offers.
Approve AI tools, monitor adverse impact and maintain jurisdictional posting rules.
Sets export-control flags on requisitions and clears flagged hires.

countryAddenda.us: Show good-faith ranges in postings covered by CO, WA, NY, IL, MN, MD, HI, DC, NJ, VT, MA, VA (Jul 1, 2026), ME (Jul 29, 2026) and CT (Oct 1, 2026, with a benefits description), and follow salary-history bans in 20+ states and cities. NYC LL 144 requires an annual bias audit and notice 10 business days before using automated employment decision tools, IL HB 3773 requires notice of AI use from Jan 1, 2026, and Colorado SB 26-189 notice and explanation duties start Jan 1, 2027; no race- or sex-restricted slates or targets.
countryAddenda.us-ca: Every posting for a role that may be filled in California, including remote and third-party postings, must show a good-faith estimate of the salary or hourly range (SB 642), and employees may request their current role's pay scale; never ask salary history (LC 432.3). CRD automated-decision system rules (Oct 1, 2025) make the Company liable for discriminatory AI tools with 4-year data retention, CCPA ADMT notice and opt-out or appeal rights start 1 Jan 2027, and applicants need a CCPA notice at collection.
countryAddenda.ca: Ontario (25+ employees): publicly advertised postings must show pay or a range (max C$50,000 spread; exempt above C$200,000), disclose AI used in screening, state whether a vacancy currently exists and not require Canadian experience; interviewed applicants must be told the outcome within 45 days, with records kept 3 years. BC: pay or a range in every public posting and no pay-history questions; offer accommodation during recruitment (AODA).
countryAddenda.in: Report vacancies to the National Career Service before filling them as required under the Social Security Code rules, and keep hiring gender-neutral (Code on Wages s.3) with no questions on caste, religion, marital or pregnancy status. Record whether each role is a 'worker' or a managerial/supervisory position and issue the statutory appointment letter at joining.
countryAddenda.tw: Postings for roles paying under NT$40,000 a month must show a salary range, and forms and interviews may not ask about marital status, pregnancy plans, horoscope, blood type or other non-job-related private information (Employment Services Act Art. 5). Run the clean-hire certification for candidates from TSMC, MediaTek, UMC and similar firms and check any existing Art. 9-1 non-compete.
countryAddenda.cn: Job ads and interviews may not use gender, marital or childbearing status, ethnicity, religion, health status or hard age caps as criteria (Employment Promotion Law; Women's Rights Law Art. 43). Collect candidate data under a PIPL notice with consent for background checks, and confirm the candidate holds a termination certificate from the prior employer and has no unexpired non-compete (LCL Art. 91).

decisions: Post pay ranges for every role globally or only where required? (Ranges on all US postings are the practical norm; Asia ranges stay optional except Taiwan roles under NT$40,000.)
Use AI resume screening for high-volume new-graduate hiring? (Requires bias testing, notices in NYC, IL, Ontario and California, and human review.)
Panel size and use of technical take-home exercises? (Take-homes must avoid real customer problems or proprietary data.)
Central sourcing team or recruiters embedded in business units?
Internal-first posting period (e.g., 5 business days) before external posting? (Supports mobility; Ontario's posting rules do not apply to internal-only postings.)
pitfalls: One global Greenhouse application form that asks for current salary, date of birth or citizenship.
Ontario postings with ranges wider than C$50,000 or no AI disclosure, and no 45-day follow-up with interviewed candidates.
Asking every candidate about citizenship 'for export control', creating 1324b and FEHA exposure.
Interviewers asking candidates to walk through a competitor's design details.
Hiring managers making verbal offers before approval.
policies.training: Structured interviewing and fair-hiring training before a first interview panel and every 2 years; annual recruiter training on jurisdictional posting, salary-history and AI rules.

policies.name: Background Screening
policies.owner: Talent Acquisition Operations with Legal (Employment and Privacy) and Security
policies.approver: CHRO + General Counsel
policies.review: Annual + on law change
policies.audience: Candidates who accept conditional offers for employee, intern and executive roles; contractors with system or lab access (through their vendors); employees moving into designated high-trust roles
policies.purpose: Verifies candidates' identity, credentials and history in proportion to the role, in line with consumer-reporting, fair-chance, privacy and anti-discrimination laws in each country. It protects trade secrets, controlled technology, finances and people while giving candidates notice, consent and a fair chance to respond.
keyProvisions: Screening starts only after a conditional offer (except identity and right-to-work checks that local law requires earlier) and only with the candidate's written notice and authorization or consent in the required local form.

Screening packages are set by role tier: Standard (identity, highest degree, 7 years of employment history, restricted-party screening); Enhanced for finance, Section 16 officers, IT and security administrators, trade compliance and roles with controlled-technology access (adds criminal record and credit checks where lawful and job-related, and professional references); Executive (adds media, regulatory and directorship checks).

Criminal history is considered only where lawful, after the conditional offer, and through an individualized assessment of the nature and gravity of the offense, time elapsed and relevance to the job; arrests without conviction are never considered.

Before any adverse decision based wholly or partly on a report, the candidate receives the report, any required statement of rights and at least 5 business days to respond; a final notice follows any adverse decision.
Credit checks are used only where lawful and job-related, such as finance roles with signing authority.

Screening never includes medical, genetic, pregnancy, hepatitis B or HIV tests or questions; any post-offer medical exam is limited to job-related needs (e.g., lab hazard exposure) and applied to everyone entering that job category.

Restricted-party screening (Entity List, SDN, UFLPA, DOJ Data Security Program covered persons) applies to all hires, contractors and interns' sponsoring institutions; potential matches are resolved by Trade Compliance and never decided by nationality or name alone.
Candidates coming from Entity List companies or direct competitors trigger enhanced trade-secret onboarding (no-bring certifications, access review), not rejection.

Background-check vendors are contracted as processors with data-protection, security and cross-border transfer terms; reports are stored separately from personnel files and accessible only to TA Operations and Legal.
Employees are re-screened, with fresh consent, on moving into an Enhanced-tier role and, where lawful, every 3 years in designated roles.
Falsified credentials discovered at any time are grounds for offer withdrawal or termination under the applicable local process.
policies.sampleLanguage:
Scope and Timing. [Company] conducts background checks after a conditional offer of employment has been made and accepted, and only with your written authorization. The checks performed depend on the role and the country and may include verification of identity, education, professional qualifications and prior employment; screening against government restricted-party lists; and, where permitted by law and relevant to the position, criminal record and credit checks.

Fairness. We consider criminal history only where the law allows and only after an individualized assessment of whether the record is relevant to the specific job, taking into account the nature of the offense and the time that has passed. We never consider arrests that did not lead to a conviction. We do not request medical, genetic or pregnancy information as part of background screening.

Your Right to Respond. If information in a background report may lead us to withdraw an offer, we will first give you a copy of the report and a summary of your rights, and at least five business days to explain or correct the information before we make a final decision.

Confidentiality. Background reports are kept confidential, stored separately from personnel files and used only for employment purposes.

roles.duties: Starts checks through the vendor after offer acceptance, issues notices and runs the adverse-action process.
Approves screening packages by country and tier, performs individualized-assessment reviews and handles disputes.
Resolves restricted-party matches and sets onboarding controls for hires from Entity List companies.
Confirms the role tier and never sees background reports.
Performs checks lawfully, secures data and supports candidate disputes.

countryAddenda.us: FCRA requires a standalone disclosure and authorization, a pre-adverse action notice with the report and CFPB Summary of Rights, a waiting period (commonly 5 business days) and an adverse action notice, plus fair-chance rules in NYC, IL, WA and elsewhere. Keep export-control questions out of Form I-9 and E-Verify, and follow ADA limits on medical inquiries until after the conditional offer.
countryAddenda.us-ca: Under the Fair Chance Act (5+ employees) there is no criminal-history inquiry before a conditional offer, then a written individualized assessment, a preliminary notice with the report and 5 business days to respond (plus 5 more if disputing) and a final notice citing the right to file with CRD. Give separate ICRAA and FCRA disclosures, limit credit checks to Labor Code 1024.5 roles (e.g., access to trade secrets or $10,000+ cash), and never ask about cannabis use or sealed or diverted records.
countryAddenda.ca: Criminal and credit checks need consent and a legitimate job requirement; in Ontario give notice under the Consumer Reporting Act, and remember that record of offences (ON) and unrelated criminal convictions (BC) are protected grounds. The candidate obtains police record checks with consent, and collection must meet BC PIPA reasonableness and notice rules.
countryAddenda.in: Use a written BGV consent and notice covering education, employment, address and criminal checks via court records or police verification; never make Aadhaar authentication mandatory, and accept only masked or voluntarily provided Aadhaar. Verify original certificates and return them the same day (Karnataka 2026 amendment); DPDP s.7(i) may cover recruitment, but keep consent until case law settles.
countryAddenda.tw: Give a PDPA notice; criminal records and health data are sensitive (PDPA Art. 6) and need written consent or a statutory basis, and checks must be job-related and proportionate. Handle the employer-paid pre-employment physical exam required by OSH Act Art. 20 as sensitive data.
countryAddenda.cn: Private employers cannot obtain official criminal-record checks, so rely on candidate declarations and permitted vendor verification under a PIPL notice with separate consent and entrusted-processing agreements with vendors. Collect the prior employer's termination certificate and check for non-compete obligations; pre-employment medicals may not include hepatitis B or pregnancy tests.

decisions: Criminal checks for all hires or Enhanced-tier roles only? (A tiered approach is easier to defend under fair-chance and privacy laws.)
One global vendor or country vendors? (A global vendor simplifies SOX evidence; confirm China data localization.)
Periodic re-screening of current employees? (Limit to designated roles, with fresh consent.)
Allow start before checks complete? (Only for Standard tier with a contingency clause; never for Enhanced-tier roles.)
Verify education for experienced hires with 10+ years of experience? (Many issuers verify the highest degree only.)
pitfalls: FCRA disclosures bundled with liability waivers or other terms, a frequent class-action trigger.
Pre-offer criminal questions in global Greenhouse forms that reach California or NYC candidates.
Rejecting candidates whose common Chinese name matches a restricted-party entry without resolving the match.
Keeping Indian candidates' original certificates or requiring Aadhaar authentication.
policies.training: Annual training for TA Operations on FCRA, fair-chance and country consent requirements; hiring-manager guidance on role tiers at manager onboarding.
