policies.name: Export Control & Deemed Exports (Employees)
policies.owner: Trade Compliance (Export Control Officer) with HR (People Ops, Talent Acquisition, Immigration) and IT/Security
policies.approver: General Counsel + Chief Compliance Officer + CHRO; Empowered Official for license matters
policies.review: Annual + on any BIS rule change affecting Company technology (e.g., advanced-computing rules; Affiliates Rule return on Nov 10, 2026)
policies.audience: All employees, interns, contractors, visiting researchers, interview candidates and visitors who may access Company technology, source code, lab equipment or systems
policies.purpose: Prevents unlicensed release of export-controlled technology and source code to foreign persons (deemed exports and deemed re-exports) while avoiding unlawful citizenship or national-origin discrimination. It ties HR events (hiring, transfers, immigration changes, assignments and exits) to technology access controls under the Company's Technology Control Plan (TCP).
keyProvisions: Trade Compliance assigns an export-control flag to each job code and requisition based on the classification (ECCN) of technology and source code the role will access; unflagged roles receive no controlled-technology access.

For flagged roles only, the recruiter asks every finalist the approved question ('Are you a U.S. person, meaning a U.S. citizen or national, lawful permanent resident, asylee or refugee? If not, list all countries of citizenship and permanent residency'); answers go on a separate export form in the Trade Compliance system, never in Form I-9 or the general HRIS record.

Start dates and provisioning of controlled repositories, EDA projects, labs and technical data depend on Trade Compliance clearance or a license; where a license is required, access stays blocked until it is granted and license provisos are tracked per person.

The Company does not limit jobs to US citizens or exclude permanent residents, asylees or refugees unless a law, regulation, executive order or government contract requires it (e.g., ITAR programs or security clearances).

Trade Compliance completes a written deemed-export assessment for every H-1B, L-1 and O-1 petition (new, extension or amendment) before the Form I-129 Part 6 certification is signed, and repeats it on any change of role, project or worksite.

HR events trigger re-screening: transfer, promotion, project change, change of immigration status or citizenship, international assignment and return; Darwinbox sends these events to Trade Compliance and identity management automatically.
Flagged employees receive a TCP briefing and sign an acknowledgment before access, with annual refreshers.
Lab tours, code demos, whiteboard sessions and interview presentations involving controlled technology are not given to foreign-person candidates or visitors without clearance.

US persons, including green-card holders, may not support development or production of advanced-node ICs at fabs in China, Macau or D:5 countries without Trade Compliance review (EAR 744.6), and departing US-person engineers joining such companies are reminded of their personal license obligations.

At exit, controlled access is revoked no later than the last day (immediately for involuntary exits), license-conditioned departures are reported as required, and export records are kept for 5 years (EAR Part 762).
Sales and FAE incentive plans give no credit for unscreened or unlicensed business, with forfeiture and clawback for violations.

Suspected unauthorized releases or diversion must be reported immediately to Trade Compliance or the Speak Up hotline; discipline and voluntary self-disclosure decisions are coordinated with Trade Compliance and Legal.
policies.sampleLanguage:
Purpose. [Company] develops technology that is subject to U.S. and other export control laws. Sharing certain technology or source code with a foreign national, even inside our own offices or through a screen share, may be an 'export' that requires a government license.

Screening for Controlled Roles. Positions that require access to export-controlled technology are identified in advance by Trade Compliance. Candidates for those positions only will be asked whether they are a U.S. person and, if not, their countries of citizenship and permanent residence. This information is used solely to determine whether an export license is needed, is kept separately from Form I-9 and other employment records, and is not used to make hiring decisions except as required by law.

Access Before Clearance. No employee, intern, contractor or visitor may receive access to controlled technology, source code, labs or systems until Trade Compliance has confirmed that access is authorized.

Your Responsibilities. You must follow the Technology Control Plan, share technical data only with people who are authorized to receive it, and report any suspected unauthorized release immediately. [Company] does not discriminate on the basis of citizenship or national origin, and export compliance is never a reason to exclude qualified candidates from roles that do not require controlled access.

roles.duties: Classifies technology, flags roles, screens and obtains licenses, runs the TCP and keeps export records for 5 years.
Asks the approved question only for flagged roles and sends answers to Trade Compliance separately from I-9 data.
Triggers re-screening on HR events and holds start dates pending clearance.
Enforces access controls tied to clearance status and revokes access at exit.
Obtains Trade Compliance's written assessment before any I-129 Part 6 certification is signed.
Request controlled access only for cleared staff and prevent informal sharing with uncleared colleagues or visitors.

countryAddenda.us: INA 274B (8 U.S.C. 1324b) and DOJ IER guidance bar citizenship-based hiring limits and document abuse justified by export control, so ask the U.S.-person question only for flagged roles, uniformly and separately from I-9 and E-Verify. If any USML items or defense services exist, ITAR requires separate program staffing, TCPs and licenses (China is subject to a policy of denial), and the DOJ Data Security Program limits China-resident staff's access to bulk US sensitive personal data.
countryAddenda.us-ca: FEHA prohibits national-origin discrimination, so ask citizenship questions only as necessary for licensing, preferably after the offer. Citizenship and immigration status are sensitive personal information under the CCPA, so state the purpose in the applicant and employee notices and limit use.
countryAddenda.ca: Releasing EAR-controlled technology to a third-country national in Toronto or Vancouver is a deemed re-export to that person's most recent country of citizenship or permanent residency. The Ontario Human Rights Code protects citizenship and both provinces protect place of origin, so restrict only where legally required; ITAR items also trigger Canada's Controlled Goods Program (verify registration needs).
countryAddenda.in: Releasing US-origin controlled technology to Indian nationals in India is a re-export to India (Country Group A:5, often license-exception eligible), but release to third-country nationals such as Chinese or Russian nationals is a deemed re-export to their home country. Screen at hire under an SPDI/DPDP-compliant notice and check India's SCOMET controls for exports from India.
countryAddenda.tw: Apply EAR deemed re-export screening and Taiwan's strategic high-tech commodities (SHTC) controls, and identify roles touching national core key technologies (e.g., AI/HPC chip design, chiplet interconnect design, ≤14nm process) for enhanced access controls under the National Security Act. Staff on government core key technology projects need approval for mainland China travel, and PRC nationals are effectively barred from Taiwan employment.
countryAddenda.cn: EAR 744.6 bars US-person staff from supporting advanced-node fabs in China without a license, Entity List customers limit which customers FAEs may support, and releasing controlled technology to PRC nationals is a deemed re-export that often needs a license. Frame restrictions as legal compliance without statements that invite Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law claims, collect nationality data under PIPL notice, and check China's Export Control Law before PRC-developed technology is transferred abroad.

decisions: When to ask the export question: at application, after interviews or after the offer? (DOJ IER favors late-stage, uniform questions for flagged roles; late screening risks start-date delays when licenses are needed.)
Hire foreign persons into flagged roles while a license is pending, assigning unrestricted work meanwhile? (Workable with strict segregation; licenses can take months.)
Scope of flagged roles: all design engineers or only teams on 3A090/4A090-class and other controlled products? (Narrow flags reduce screening burden and discrimination risk.)
Where to keep export records: Trade Compliance system or restricted HRIS fields? (A separate system is recommended.)
Rules for candidate lab tours and interview presentations? (Default: no controlled content.)
pitfalls: Posting 'US citizens only' or 'must be a US person' without a legal or contract requirement.
Signing I-129 Part 6 from an outside-counsel template without Trade Compliance's analysis of actual access.
No re-screening when an employee moves from an unrestricted team to an advanced AI/HPC product team.
Granting repository access on Day 1 through default group memberships before clearance.
Treating prior employment at an Entity List company as disqualifying instead of as a trigger for trade-secret onboarding.
policies.training: TCP briefing and signed acknowledgment before controlled access; annual role-based export training for engineering, FAE, sales, support, TA and Immigration staff, delivered in local language in China, Taiwan and India.

policies.name: Immigration Sponsorship
policies.owner: Immigration (Global Mobility) with Talent Acquisition and Legal
policies.approver: CHRO + General Counsel; CFO for fee-policy decisions (e.g., the H-1B $100,000 payment or proposed cap-petition fee)
policies.review: Annual + immediately on major rule changes (US H-1B fee litigation and rulemaking, prevailing-wage rule, Canadian levels plan)
policies.audience: Candidates and employees who need work authorization in any Company location; hiring managers and recruiters
policies.purpose: Sets when and how the Company sponsors work authorization and permanent residence, who pays, and how sponsorship interacts with hiring, pay, export control and RIFs. It keeps the Company compliant with employer duties under each country's immigration regime while managing the sharply higher cost and uncertainty of US H-1B sponsorship in 2026-27.
keyProvisions: The Company sponsors temporary work authorization where business need is documented and the candidate is the best qualified applicant; sponsorship eligibility (yes, no or case-by-case) is recorded on each requisition and applied consistently.
Sponsorship decisions use job-related criteria; the Company neither prefers visa holders over US or local workers nor excludes work-authorized non-citizens, except as the law permits.
The Company pays all employer-required costs, including government filing fees and attorney fees for employer petitions (H-1B, PERM, LMIA, work permits), and never recovers them from employees.

New H-1B cap petitions, or petitions for beneficiaries outside the US that could trigger the Proclamation 10973 payment or any future DHS cap-petition fee, require CFO and CHRO approval before an offer commits to them.
Immigration obtains Trade Compliance's deemed-export assessment before any petition requiring the Form I-129 Part 6 certification.
US green-card (PERM) sponsorship begins for eligible employees in good standing after [12] months of employment (earlier for senior or O-1-eligible hires), subject to business need.
Offer letters for sponsored hires state that employment depends on obtaining and keeping work authorization and that start dates may move.

Changes to a sponsored employee's duties, worksite (including remote location), hours or pay must be reviewed by Immigration before they take effect so amendments, new LCAs or updated permits can be filed.

Before any RIF, Immigration reviews the effect on sponsored employees and pending petitions, including bona fide termination steps and the Sept 18, 2026 executive order directing agencies to weigh layoffs in H-1B decisions.
Employees keep Immigration informed of status changes; Immigration diarizes document expiries at least 180 days ahead.
Immigration compliance records (LCA public access files, permits, IRCC offer records) are retained as each country requires (e.g., Canada 6 years).
policies.sampleLanguage:
Sponsorship Eligibility. [Company] may sponsor work authorization when a position requires skills the business needs and the selected candidate is the best qualified applicant. Whether a position is eligible for sponsorship is decided when the requisition is approved and is applied consistently to all candidates for that position. Sponsorship is not available for every role, and we cannot guarantee that any petition will be approved.

Costs. [Company] pays all government filing fees and legal fees that the law requires an employer to pay for employer-sponsored petitions and applications. We will never ask you to repay these costs.

Changes to Your Job. Because your immigration status may depend on your job duties, work location and salary, do not change your role, work location or working hours until Immigration has confirmed that the change is permitted or that any required filing has been made.

Permanent Residence. Employees in good standing may be considered for permanent residence sponsorship after [twelve] months of employment, subject to business needs and eligibility requirements.

Your Responsibilities. You must provide accurate information, tell Immigration about any change in your status and notify us well before any document expires.

roles.duties: Assesses options, manages counsel and filings, keeps compliance files and tracks expiries.
Records sponsorship eligibility on requisitions and states contingencies in offers.
Justify the business need for sponsorship and plan for start-date uncertainty.
Provides written deemed-export assessments for petitions.
Keep wages at or above required or offered levels throughout sponsorship.
Oversees RIF impacts and non-discrimination compliance.

countryAddenda.us: H-1B cap registration (March) now uses wage-weighted selection (Level IV gets 4 entries); the $100,000 payment for beneficiaries abroad is vacated (D. Mass., June 8, 2026) but the proclamation was extended to Sept 21, 2027, and DHS proposed a $103,265 fee on cap-subject petitions (NPRM Aug 25, 2026). The employer must bear H-1B attorney and ACWIA fees and PERM costs (20 CFR 655.731, 656.12), keep LCA public access files and pay required wages; STEM OPT hires need E-Verify and a Form I-983, and DOL has proposed higher prevailing-wage levels (Mar 2026).
countryAddenda.us-ca: Follow the US federal addendum; in addition, AB 692 bars repayment clauses for agreements from 1 Jan 2026, so do not use immigration-cost repayment agreements for California employees (monitor AB 1697 amendments).
countryAddenda.ca: Preferred routes are intra-company transfer (LMIA-exempt), CUSMA Professional for US and Mexican engineers, and the Global Talent Stream (10-business-day LMIA standard); for LMIA-exempt hires submit the offer in the IRCC Employer Portal, pay the C$230 compliance fee, keep records 6 years and honor the offer terms. Temporary-worker arrivals are capped at 230,000 a year (2026-28), and since Jan 21, 2025 spousal open work permits require the principal to hold a TEER 0/1 (or listed TEER 2/3) role with 16+ months left.
countryAddenda.in: Foreign nationals need an Employment (E) visa, generally with salary above USD 25,000 a year, and must register with the FRRO within 14 days of arrival for stays of 180+ days under the Immigration and Foreigners Act 2025 (verify employer reporting duties). International workers contribute to EPF on full salary unless covered by a social security agreement certificate.
countryAddenda.tw: Obtain a WDA work permit for specialized work (salary threshold about NT$47,971 a month; verify) or use the Employment Gold Card; the 2026 Foreign Professionals Act amendments widened eligibility for graduates of top universities and eased spouses' work rights. PRC nationals are effectively barred from employment.
countryAddenda.cn: Obtain the Foreigner's Work Permit (A/B/C tier), Z visa and residence permit (within 30 days of entry) before work starts; foreign employees' contracts may not exceed 5 years, and SPC Interpretation II Art. 4 recognizes employment only with valid permits or permanent residence. Enroll foreign employees in social insurance.

decisions: Which roles are sponsorship-eligible: all professional roles or hard-to-fill engineering roles only?
Absorb the H-1B $100,000 payment or proposed $103,265 fee, or shift hiring to Canada, India or Taiwan hubs? (Model per role and consider O-1 and L-1 alternatives.)
When to start PERM: at hire, after 6 months or after 12 months? (Earlier starts aid retention; PERM costs are employer-borne.)
Offer above the required wage level to improve weighted-lottery odds? (Level III/IV offers raise selection chances.)
Repayment agreements for voluntary (non-required) immigration costs? (Not allowed for employer-required fees and restricted in California; generally avoid.)
pitfalls: Passing H-1B attorney fees or PERM costs to employees, which DOL rules prohibit.
Moving a sponsored employee to a new worksite or remote location without an LCA or amendment.
Announcing a RIF without assessing H-1B and pending PERM impacts.
Applying 'no sponsorship' statements inconsistently across postings, inviting discrimination claims.
policies.training: Annual briefing for recruiters and hiring managers on sponsorship criteria and non-discrimination; Immigration team updates as rules change.

policies.name: Contingent Workforce & Worker Classification
policies.owner: People Ops (Contingent Workforce Program) with Procurement and Legal
policies.approver: CHRO + CFO + General Counsel
policies.review: Annual + on law change (US contractor rule, India Labour Code state rules)
policies.audience: Managers engaging independent contractors, consultants, agency temps, dispatch workers, employer-of-record (EOR) workers and statement-of-work vendors; Procurement and HR
policies.purpose: Ensures non-employee workers are engaged through the right channel, correctly classified, screened for export-control and sanctions risk, and managed without creating misclassification or co-employment liability. It covers independent contractors, staffing-agency workers, labor dispatch, EOR arrangements and SOW services.
keyProvisions: Every contingent engagement requires a request with business justification, budget approval, a classification assessment and a signed Company-approved agreement before work starts.

People Ops applies the classification test of the work location (ABC test where applicable, economic-reality or core-factor test, local employment-relationship tests) using a documented questionnaire; core, ongoing, directed and integrated work is filled by employees or through a compliant agency or EOR.

Independent contractors must run their own business, control how the work is done and invoice for deliverables; they may not supervise employees, have direct reports, receive employee benefits or equity, or hold Company job titles.
Individual contractor engagements are limited to 12 months, renewable once after a fresh classification review; any engagement beyond 24 months needs CHRO approval.

Agency and dispatch workers are supervised by their provider for employment matters (pay, discipline, leave); Company managers direct day-to-day work only as the contract allows and do not interview, hire or terminate them directly unless local law permits.

All contingent workers undergo restricted-party screening and, where they need controlled technology, the same export clearance as employees; access is provisioned through identity management with an end date.

Contingent workers sign confidentiality and IP assignment terms (with the DTSA notice for the US) before access and complete required security, harassment and safety training; they may use Speak Up channels.
Suppliers certify compliance with wage, hours, social insurance and anti-trafficking laws and the Human Rights policy, including no recruitment fees.
Former employees may be re-engaged as contractors only after 6 months and with HR approval.
Access is revoked on the engagement end date, and managers confirm return of assets and data.
People Ops reports contingent headcount, tenure and spend by country quarterly and reviews long-tenure engagements for conversion.
policies.sampleLanguage:
Engaging Non-Employee Workers. [Company] uses independent contractors, consultants, agency workers and service providers to meet specialized or temporary needs. Before any non-employee begins work, the hiring manager must submit a contingent workforce request, and People Ops, Procurement and Legal must approve the engagement type and contract. No one may start work, receive system or lab access, or be paid without an approved engagement.

Classification. Whether someone is an employee depends on the law of the place where the work is performed and on how the work is actually done, not on the title of the contract. Individuals who perform ongoing work under the direction of a [Company] manager, as part of our core business, generally must be engaged as employees or through an approved staffing provider.

Managing Contingent Workers. Managers may assign and review the work of contingent workers but must not treat them as employees: do not give them employee titles, direct reports, employee benefits, performance reviews or discipline. Employment matters for agency workers must be handled by their agency.

Compliance. All contingent workers must be screened, sign confidentiality and intellectual property terms, and complete required training before receiving access to Company systems, labs or technology.

roles.duties: Request engagements, define deliverables and avoid treating contingent workers as employees.
Performs classification assessments, tracks tenure and triggers conversion reviews.
Contracts suppliers with compliance, audit and data-protection terms.
Decides borderline classifications and local labor-dispatch compliance.
Screen workers and provision and revoke access by end date.

countryAddenda.us: DOL's Feb 26, 2026 proposal would restore the 2021 core-factor test (control and opportunity for profit or loss); state ABC tests (e.g., MA, NJ, IL for some purposes) are stricter, and the Form 1099-NEC threshold rose to $2,000 for payments after Dec 31, 2025. Joint-employer exposure arises where managers direct staffing-agency workers.
countryAddenda.us-ca: Labor Code 2775 (AB 5) applies the ABC test for most purposes: a worker is an employee unless free from control, performing work outside the usual course of the business and customarily engaged in an independent business; misclassification brings wage, expense-reimbursement (LC 2802) and PAGA exposure. Employers using 100+ workers through labor contractors must file a separate CRD pay data report.
countryAddenda.ca: CRA assesses CPP and EI on disguised employment, and Ontario courts award reasonable notice to dependent contractors (Keenan v. Canac Kitchens, 2016 ONCA 79); Ontario's temporary help agency rules can make the client liable for certain unpaid wages (verify). A Quebec-based contractor triggers French-language and Quebec labour-standards review.
countryAddenda.in: Contract labour is now regulated under the OSH Code (contractor licensing and principal-employer duties above prescribed thresholds, and limits on contract labour in core activities; verify thresholds and state rules), and the principal employer is liable for contract workers' unpaid wages and social security. Individual consultants integrated into engineering teams risk being treated as 'workers' with retrenchment and gratuity rights.
countryAddenda.tw: Dispatched workers are employed by the dispatch agency; the user company may not interview or select specific dispatched workers in advance (otherwise the worker may request direct employment) and has supplementary liability for unpaid wages and occupational injury (LSA Arts. 17-1, 22-1, 63-1; verify). Contractor or fixed-term arrangements for ongoing work are converted to indefinite employment.
countryAddenda.cn: Local staff must be employed by the WFOE or through licensed dispatch or HR agencies; dispatched workers may fill only temporary, auxiliary or substitute positions, may not exceed 10% of total workforce and must receive equal pay for equal work (LCL Arts. 63, 66). Individual 'consultants' doing ongoing work risk a de facto labor relationship with double-wage and open-ended contract exposure.

decisions: Engage contingent labor through a managed service provider or decentralized procurement? (An MSP improves tenure tracking and classification control.)
Maximum tenure for contractors and agency workers: 12, 18 or 24 months?
Use an EOR for single hires in new countries or set up an entity? (EOR is faster but raises permanent-establishment and control questions.)
Allow contractors access to controlled technology? (Only with export clearance and a TCP acknowledgment.)
Agency conversion fees and non-solicitation terms?
pitfalls: Long-tenured California 'contractors' doing core engineering under manager direction, failing the ABC test.
Company managers interviewing and choosing Taiwan dispatch workers, triggering direct-employment claims.
Exceeding China's 10% dispatch cap or using dispatch for core engineering roles.
Contractors reaching controlled technology through shared accounts without export screening.
Contractor accounts with no end dates, leaving access active after engagements end.
policies.training: Guidance on engaging contingent workers for every new people manager; annual refresher for Procurement and People Ops on classification tests by country.

policies.name: Probation & Confirmation
policies.owner: HR Business Partners (process) with People Ops (tracking)
policies.approver: CHRO; local legal review of probation terms for Canada, India, Taiwan and China
policies.review: Every 2 years + on law change
policies.audience: New hires (employees) and their managers; internal transfers only where local law and contract allow
policies.purpose: Defines how the Company uses an initial assessment period to confirm new hires' capability, fit and conduct, with structured check-ins and documented confirmation. Because probation has very different legal effects by country (none in the US, statutory limits in China, notice consequences in Canada and Taiwan), the policy sets global expectations and defers to local rules.
keyProvisions: Each new hire's probation or introductory period is stated in the offer or contract where local law allows: US introductory period of 90 days (no change to at-will status); Canada 3 months; India 6 months; Taiwan 3 months; China per the statutory maximum for the contract term.
Within the first 2 weeks, managers set written 30-60-90 day goals in the onboarding plan, including measurable role criteria that will be used to assess confirmation.
Managers hold documented check-ins at 30, 60 and (where applicable) 90 days, recording feedback and support in Darwinbox.
At least 15 days before probation ends, the manager recommends confirm, extend (where lawful) or end employment, with evidence, to the HRBP.
Confirmation is issued in writing where local practice requires; otherwise employment continues automatically at the end of the period.
Probation may be extended once, by no more than the original length, only where local law and the contract allow and before the original period ends, with written reasons and an improvement plan.

Ending employment during or at the end of probation requires HRBP and Legal review and must follow local notice, severance and procedural rules; it may never be based on protected characteristics, leave or accommodation requests.
Probation does not delay statutory entitlements such as social insurance enrollment or sick-leave accrual unless local law provides, and US benefits waiting periods may not exceed 90 days.
Export-control clearance, background-check completion and IP agreements are pre-start requirements, not probation items.
Internal transfers and promotions carry no new probation period unless local law allows it and the employee agrees.
policies.sampleLanguage:
Introductory Period. Your first months at [Company] are an opportunity for you and your manager to confirm that the role is a good fit. Your offer letter or employment contract states the length of your introductory or probation period, which depends on the country where you work. During this period your manager will agree goals with you within your first two weeks, meet with you regularly to review progress and provide the support you need to succeed.

Confirmation. Before the end of the period, your manager will review your performance against the agreed goals. If your performance meets expectations, your employment will be confirmed in writing where that is local practice. In some cases, and only where permitted by local law and your contract, the period may be extended once so that you have more time to meet expectations; if so, you will be told why in writing.

Your Rights. The introductory period does not reduce any rights you have under local law. In the United States, completing an introductory period does not change the at-will nature of employment.

roles.duties: Set measurable goals, hold documented check-ins and make a timely, evidence-based recommendation.
Reviews recommendations, applies local legal requirements and issues confirmation or extension letters.
Tracks probation end dates in Darwinbox and sends reminders 30 and 15 days before the end date.
Reviews any termination during probation outside the US.
Engage with goals and feedback and raise support needs early.

countryAddenda.us: There is no statutory probation; state that completing an introductory period creates no for-cause protection (Montana's WDEA is the exception if any Montana employees are hired). The ACA limits benefits waiting periods to 90 days.
countryAddenda.us-ca: Call it an 'introductory period' and confirm it does not change at-will status (Labor Code 2922); paid sick leave may be used after 90 days, and CFRA eligibility runs on its own 12-month and 1,250-hour schedule.
countryAddenda.ca: Ontario ESA notice and BC compensation for length of service start only after 3 months, but a contractual probation clause must clearly limit notice or common-law reasonable notice applies, and suitability must be assessed in good faith. The contract containing the probation clause must be signed before the start date.
countryAddenda.in: Market practice is 3-6 months, extendable once, with a written confirmation letter; where standing orders apply (300+ workers) their probation terms govern workers. Set 7-30 days' notice during probation in the appointment letter and document performance before any non-confirmation.
countryAddenda.tw: Probation is not statutory: ending employment during or at the end of it still needs an LSA Art. 11 or 12 ground (usually Art. 11(5) incompetence), with Art. 16 notice once service reaches 3 months and pro-rated severance. Record objective written criteria and coaching to meet the courts' last-resort test.
countryAddenda.cn: Maximum probation is 1 month for contracts of 3 months to under 1 year, 2 months for 1 to under 3 years, and 6 months for 3+ years or open-ended contracts; only one probation per employee per employer, and pay must be at least 80% of the agreed wage and not below minimum wage (LCL Arts. 19-21). Dismissal during probation needs documented failure of hiring criteria disclosed and acknowledged in advance, communicated before probation ends.

decisions: Use a probation period in the US at all? (Many US employers drop it to avoid implying for-cause protection afterwards.)
Standard length by country, or by level (e.g., 6 months for senior hires in India)?
Allow extensions? (Useful in India; not possible in China beyond the statutory maximum and one-probation rule.)
Automatic confirmation or a required confirmation letter? (A letter is expected in India; automatic elsewhere avoids administrative lapses.)
Probation on internal transfer? (Generally no; consent-based where lawful.)
pitfalls: Treating the end of probation in Taiwan or China as a free exit without statutory grounds, notice or severance.
Missing China's deadline by not communicating non-confirmation before probation ends.
US offer letters promising 'permanent' status after probation.
No documented goals or check-ins, leaving no evidence of unsuitability.
policies.training: Manager guidance delivered through Darwinbox prompts for each new hire; HRBP training on country probation rules every 2 years.

policies.name: Early Careers & Internships
policies.owner: Talent Acquisition (University Programs)
policies.approver: CHRO; General Counsel for internship agreements and immigration terms
policies.review: Annual, before each campus season (August)
policies.audience: Interns, co-op students, apprentices, new-graduate hires and their managers and mentors
policies.purpose: Governs how the Company recruits, pays, manages and converts interns and new graduates, a key pipeline for VLSI, verification, physical design and embedded roles. It keeps programs open to all, paid and lawful in each country, protected against anti-corruption and export-control risks, and planned around student immigration timelines.
keyProvisions: All interns are paid at least the applicable minimum wage and at the Company's intern pay scale by degree level and location; unpaid internships are not permitted.
Interns are employees of the Company (or of an approved agency where local practice requires) with fixed start and end dates, a named manager and mentor, and a written project plan agreed in week 1.

Programs are filled only through open application; eligibility is based on field of study, graduation date and work-authorization requirements, not protected characteristics, and requests from customers, officials or partners to place candidates are declined and reported to Ethics & Compliance.

Interns follow the same export-control screening, background-screening tier, confidentiality and IP terms and training as employees in comparable roles, and do not access controlled technology before clearance.

Intern projects may not use customer-confidential data unless covered by the customer NDA and approved by Legal, and may not rely on the intern's university IP; academic publications from internship work go through the standard publication review.
Hours are recorded for non-exempt interns and overtime is paid; students under 18 are not assigned night work or hazardous lab tasks.
Return-offer decisions are made through a calibrated review at least 4 weeks before the internship ends, and offers remain open for at least 3 weeks.
New-graduate offers set start dates that allow for OPT, work permits or relocation, and contain no repayment obligations that local law prohibits.
Intern relocation and housing support follows the program guide and is never subject to repayment.
University partnerships (sponsored research, career fairs, scholarships) are screened for restricted parties and research-security concerns before engagement.
policies.sampleLanguage:
Our Programs. [Company] offers paid internships, co-op placements and new-graduate programs to students and recent graduates in engineering, business and other disciplines. Every intern is paid and receives a defined project, a manager and a mentor.

Open to All. Our programs are open to all students who meet the job-related requirements for the role, such as field of study, expected graduation date and ability to meet work-authorization requirements. We do not accept requests from customers, government officials or business partners to place particular students, and all candidates go through the same selection process.

Same Rules as Employees. Interns must follow all Company policies, including the Code of Business Conduct, the Technology Control Plan and confidentiality obligations. Interns will not be given access to export-controlled technology until Trade Compliance approves.

Conversion. We aim to make return-offer decisions at least four weeks before the internship ends, based on a consistent review of each intern's performance and business needs. New-graduate offers will reflect realistic start dates, taking into account any immigration or academic requirements.

roles.duties: Plans headcount, campus strategy, intern pay scales and conversion calibration.
Provide a real project and weekly feedback, record non-exempt intern hours and give timely return-offer input.
Advises on CPT, OPT, STEM OPT and permit timelines for interns and new graduates.
Screens interns in flagged roles and university partners for restricted parties.
Reviews external placement requests and university relationships for corruption risk.

countryAddenda.us: Paying all interns avoids reliance on the FLSA 'primary beneficiary' test for unpaid internships, and most interns are non-exempt, needing timekeeping and overtime. STEM OPT requires E-Verify and a Form I-983 training plan, and DHS's F-1 fixed-admission rule (effective Sept 15, 2026) may require an I-539 alongside the I-765, so build start-date buffers; fellowships may not be restricted by race or sex.
countryAddenda.us-ca: Pay at least the local minimum wage (e.g., Sunnyvale $19.50, Mountain View $19.70, San Jose $18.45 in 2026) and treat most interns as non-exempt with daily overtime and meal and rest breaks. AB 692 bars repayment of relocation or sign-on amounts for agreements from 1 Jan 2026 except under narrow standalone exceptions.
countryAddenda.ca: School-authorized co-op placements may fall outside the Ontario ESA (verify), but paid internships must meet minimum wage (ON C$17.95 from Oct 1, 2026; BC C$18.25) and vacation pay. Screen university research partners and Mitacs interns under the federal Policy on Sensitive Technology Research and Affiliations of Concern.
countryAddenda.in: Interns and trainees are covered by the POSH Act, so include them in Internal Committee awareness, and engage apprentices under the Apprentices Act where used (verify). Campus offers should state stipend, duration and conversion terms, and any joining-bonus clawback for new graduates must be reasonable and pro-rated.
countryAddenda.tw: Interns working under Company direction are generally employees under the LSA, owed at least NT$29,500 a month or NT$196 an hour and enrolled in Labor Insurance and NHI; school-arranged internships follow student-internship rules and tripartite agreements (verify). The 2026 Foreign Professionals Act amendments ease hiring of graduates from top universities.
countryAddenda.cn: University students on internships are generally not in a labor relationship: use a written internship agreement (often tripartite with the school), pay an allowance and buy accident insurance (verify local rules). New graduates commonly sign a tripartite employment agreement before graduation, followed by a labor contract within one month of starting.

decisions: Intern pay: market rates by degree level or one flat rate? (Market rates by level are standard; publish ranges where required.)
Conversion target (e.g., 60% of eligible interns) and headcount reserved for return offers?
Sponsor H-1B for new graduates given the 2026-27 fee landscape? (Consider Canada and India alternatives.)
Housing stipend or corporate housing for interns?
Target-school list or open virtual events? (Open events support the open-to-all posture.)
pitfalls: Customer or partner 'requests' to hire an executive's child as an intern.
Giving interns repository access before export clearance because they 'start with the team'.
Treating California interns as exempt or ignoring local minimum wages.
Late return-offer decisions that lose candidates to competitors.
policies.training: Intern onboarding in week 1 covers the Code, TCP, confidentiality, harassment prevention and lab safety; manager and mentor briefing before each cohort.

policies.name: Compensation Philosophy & Pay Administration
policies.owner: Total Rewards
policies.approver: Compensation Committee (philosophy, peer group and executive pay); CHRO + CFO (broad-based pay administration and approval authorities)
policies.review: Annual (Compensation Committee re-affirms the philosophy); salary ranges refreshed annually
policies.audience: All employees; managers, HRBPs and Total Rewards staff who make or approve pay decisions
policies.purpose: States how the Company positions pay against the market, balances cash and equity for an engineering-heavy workforce, and governs and documents pay decisions. It links pay to job level and performance, supports pay-equity and transparency obligations, and keeps decisions within budget and approval authority.
keyProvisions: The Company targets total direct compensation (base, target bonus, equity) at the [60th] percentile of the semiconductor and technology peer market for each job, level and location, with base salary at about the [50th] percentile and greater weight on equity for senior engineering roles.
Every job is mapped to the global job architecture (family and level) and has a location-specific salary range (typically 80-120% of midpoint), refreshed annually from at least two survey sources.
Pay decisions are based on job level, skills, performance, market data and internal equity, never on protected characteristics or prior salary history.
New-hire offers are made within range; offers above the 75th percentile of range, or above maximum, need Total Rewards and VP approval with a documented reason.
Annual merit, promotion and equity-refresh budgets are approved by the CFO and CHRO (Compensation Committee for executives) and allocated through the comp planning tool with calibrated guidelines.
Off-cycle increases (retention, counteroffers, equity adjustments) need HRBP and Total Rewards approval; counteroffers above 10% also need VP approval.
Promotion increases typically fall between 5% and 15% and bring pay to at least the minimum of the new range.
Pay changes take effect only after documented approval in Darwinbox; Payroll processes only approved system transactions, never email or verbal instructions.
Employees may discuss their pay, and managers may not discourage or retaliate against pay discussions.
Executive officer pay is set by the Compensation Committee with an independent consultant, and CEO pay is decided without the CEO present.
Total Rewards runs a privileged pay-equity review before each annual cycle and feeds adjustments into the cycle.
policies.sampleLanguage:
Our Pay Philosophy. [Company] competes for world-class engineering and business talent. We aim to provide total compensation, combining base salary, variable pay and equity, that is competitive with the semiconductor and technology companies we compete with for talent, and that rewards performance and long-term value creation.

How Pay Is Set. Each position is assigned to a job family and level in our global job architecture. Salary ranges are set for each level and location using market data and are reviewed every year. Where your pay falls within the range depends on your skills, experience, performance and internal equity. We do not consider salary history or any protected characteristic in setting pay.

Governance. Pay decisions must follow the approval authorities set by Total Rewards and must be entered and approved in our HR system before they take effect. Executive compensation is approved by the Compensation Committee of the Board.

Transparency. We publish pay ranges where required and encourage managers to explain how pay decisions are made. You are free to discuss your own pay with others.

roles.duties: Approves the philosophy, peer group and executive officer pay, advised by an independent consultant.
Maintains job architecture, ranges, guidelines and approval authorities, and runs the annual cycle and pay-equity review.
Recommend pay within guidelines and explain decisions to employees.
Challenges outliers and approves off-cycle adjustments within delegated authority, with documentation.
Sets budgets and validates the cost of pay programs.
Processes only approved, system-generated pay changes.

countryAddenda.us: FLSA exemption requires at least $684 a week plus the duties test (higher state thresholds apply), and non-discretionary bonuses must be included in the regular rate for non-exempt staff. From 2027, IRC 162(m) adds the five highest-paid other employees to the $1M deduction cap, which can capture large RSU vests of non-officer engineers.
countryAddenda.us-ca: Exempt roles must pay at least $70,304 in 2026 ($72,384 in 2027) and computer professionals at least $58.85 an hour or $122,573.13 a year (2026); SB 642 counts bonuses, stock and benefits as 'wages' under the Equal Pay Act. Provide the pay scale for an employee's current role on request (LC 432.3).
countryAddenda.ca: Unilateral pay cuts or structural changes can amount to constructive dismissal (Potter, 2015 SCC 10), so make reductions with consent and consideration or reasonable working notice. Vacation pay of 4% (6% after 5 years) applies to non-discretionary bonuses and commissions.
countryAddenda.in: Structure CTC so basic plus DA is at least 50% of remuneration (Code on Wages s.2(y)), or accept higher PF, gratuity, leave-encashment and retrenchment costs; the mandatory EPF wage ceiling rose to INR 25,000 a month from 17 Sep 2026. Most engineers now use the new tax regime, which reduces the value of allowance structuring.
countryAddenda.tw: LSA Art. 29 requires a bonus or profit share for fault-free employees when the business makes a net profit, and the Taiwan entity's articles must state an employee-compensation percentage of profit (Company Act Art. 235-1); benchmark against TSMC and MediaTek profit-sharing worth many months of base pay. Overtime must be paid for all roles not specially designated, so model overtime-inclusive total cash.
countryAddenda.cn: Pay reductions or structural changes require written agreement (LCL Art. 35), and unilateral cuts let employees resign with severance (Art. 38). Model the separate taxation option for annual bonuses (through 31 Dec 2027) and social insurance bases (Shanghai RMB 7,546-37,731 from 1 Jul 2026) when setting cash mix.

decisions: Market position: base at P50 with total compensation at P60-75 through equity, or P50 across all elements?
US geographic pay: location-based ranges or national ranges for remote staff? (Location-based is typical; ranges must match posted ranges.)
Range width (e.g., 80-120% of midpoint) and whether to use zones within ranges?
Publish full salary ranges internally to all employees? (The trend is toward full transparency; clean up ranges first.)
Cash versus equity mix for India and China hubs, where RSU perception, tax and FX rules differ?
pitfalls: Offer exceptions that place new hires above tenured peers, creating compression and pay-equity problems.
Posted ranges that do not match the internal ranges used for offers.
Unilateral pay cuts in Canada or China.
Ignoring India's 50% wages rule after the Labour Codes, underfunding statutory liabilities.
policies.training: Manager pay-decision training before each annual cycle; HRBPs acknowledge approval authorities annually.

policies.name: Pay Equity & Pay Transparency
policies.owner: Total Rewards with Employment Legal and HR Analytics
policies.approver: CHRO + General Counsel; results reported to the Compensation Committee annually
policies.review: Annual + on law change (multiple US state, California and Canadian provincial changes in 2026-27)
policies.audience: All employees and applicants; recruiters, managers and Total Rewards
policies.purpose: Commits the Company to equal pay for equal or substantially similar work, and for work of equal value where local law requires, and sets the rules for pay ranges in postings, internal range access, pay discussions and statutory pay reporting. It establishes an annual privileged pay-equity audit with remediation and makes sure statutory pay reports are accurate and filed on time.
keyProvisions: Pay (base, bonus, commissions, equity and benefits) for equal or substantially similar work, or work of equal value where local law applies, may differ only because of documented, job-related factors such as seniority, merit, quantity or quality of output, location or skills.
Total Rewards runs an annual pay-equity analysis by country under attorney-client privilege, covering base, bonus and equity, using regression and cohort reviews of comparable roles.
Unexplained gaps are remediated in the annual cycle or by off-cycle adjustment within 6 months from a dedicated budget; pay is never reduced to remediate.
Job postings show pay ranges where the law requires and for all US roles, and ranges must be good-faith estimates of expected pay at hire.
Recruiters may not request or rely on salary history; offers are based on the role's range and job-related factors.
Employees may request the pay range for their current role and receive it within 10 business days or any shorter statutory deadline.
Employees may discuss, disclose and ask about pay without retaliation.

Statutory pay reports (California pay data, BC pay transparency report, Illinois Equal Pay Registration Certificate, Massachusetts demographic report) are prepared by HR Analytics, reviewed by Legal and filed on time, with demographic data stored separately from personnel files.
Managers record the rationale for starting pay and off-cycle adjustments in the comp planning tool.
Aggregate results and remediation spend are reported to the CHRO and the Compensation Committee annually.
policies.sampleLanguage:
Equal Pay. [Company] pays employees fairly for the work they do. Employees who perform equal or substantially similar work, or work of equal value where local law requires, will receive equal pay unless differences are explained by legitimate, job-related factors such as experience, performance, skills or work location. 'Pay' includes salary, bonuses, commissions, equity and benefits.

Pay Transparency. We include pay ranges in job postings where required by law and for all positions in the United States. We do not ask candidates about their salary history. You may ask HR for the pay range for your current role, and you are free to discuss your pay with anyone. We will not retaliate against anyone for doing so.

Monitoring. Each year [Company] reviews pay across comparable roles, with the assistance of legal counsel, to identify differences that are not explained by legitimate factors. Where we find unexplained differences, we will make adjustments. We will never reduce anyone's pay to achieve equity.

roles.duties: Maintains ranges, runs the annual audit with counsel and implements remediation.
Directs the privileged analysis, approves methodology and reviews statutory filings.
Prepares data sets and statutory pay reports and keeps demographic data separate.
Publish compliant ranges and never ask about salary history.
Set pay within range with documented rationale and answer range requests.

countryAddenda.us: The federal Equal Pay Act applies regardless of employer size, and state laws (NY, MA, IL, CO, WA, NJ, MD, OR) use 'substantially similar' or broader comparators; Illinois requires an Equal Pay Registration Certificate (100+ IL employees, every 2 years) and Massachusetts an annual demographic report by Feb 1 (100+ MA employees). Base remediation on documented analysis, not demographic targets, to avoid Title VII claims (Ames v. Ohio, 2025).
countryAddenda.us-ca: SB 642 (2026) defines pay scale as a good-faith estimate, extends the Equal Pay Act to 'another sex' as well as race and ethnicity, counts bonuses, stock, options and benefits as wages, and allows claims within 3 years with recovery back 6 years. Employers with 100+ employees file the CRD pay data report by the second Wednesday of May (12 May 2027 uses 23 SOC-based job categories), with mandatory penalties under SB 464 and a separate labor-contractor report.
countryAddenda.ca: Ontario's Pay Equity Act (10+ employees) requires maintaining pay equity between female and male job classes of comparable value, ESA s.42 requires equal pay for substantially the same work, and postings at 25+ employees need ranges with a spread of no more than C$50,000. BC requires pay in every public posting, bans pay-history questions and reprisal for pay discussions, and employers with 50+ BC employees must publish a gender pay-gap report by Nov 1, 2026 and annually after.
countryAddenda.in: Code on Wages s.3 prohibits gender (including transgender) discrimination in wages for the same or similar work and in recruitment and conditions of employment, so audit bonus and equity as well as CTC. There is no pay-range posting duty.
countryAddenda.tw: GEEA Art. 10 requires equal pay for work of equal value regardless of gender, with complaints heard by the local gender equality committee, and postings for roles paying under NT$40,000 a month must show a salary range (Employment Services Act Art. 5).
countryAddenda.cn: Equal pay for equal work applies, including to dispatched workers (LCL Art. 63), and the Women's Rights Law (2022) bars gender pay discrimination; there is no posting-range duty. Pay-audit data is personal information under PIPL, so minimize data exported to the US.

decisions: Audit scope: base only or total compensation including equity? (California now counts stock and benefits as wages; audit total compensation.)
Privileged or non-privileged audit? (Privileged under counsel direction is standard.)
Share internal ranges with all employees or only on request?
Remediation budget (e.g., 0.2-0.5% of payroll) separate from the merit budget?
Disclose pay-equity results externally? (Investor interest versus litigation risk.)
pitfalls: Posting ranges far wider than actual hiring ranges, now challenged under SB 642 and capped at C$50,000 in Ontario.
Auditing base pay only while equity grants drive most gaps for senior engineers.
Missing BC's first pay transparency report due Nov 1, 2026 for employers with 50+ BC employees.
Keeping California pay-data demographics in personnel files contrary to SB 464.
policies.training: Annual recruiter and manager training on pay transparency and salary-history bans; manager guidance before each comp cycle.

policies.name: Variable Pay & Bonus
policies.owner: Total Rewards with Finance (FP&A)
policies.approver: Compensation Committee (plan design, goals, funding and executive awards); CHRO + CFO (broad-based plan administration)
policies.review: Annual, before each plan year
policies.audience: All employees eligible for the annual bonus plan and other variable pay; sales incentive plans are governed by the Sales Compensation Governance policy
policies.purpose: Governs the design, funding, eligibility, calculation and payment of the annual bonus and other variable pay (spot awards, retention bonuses, patent awards) so they align with company performance, comply with local law and are auditable for SOX and clawback purposes.
keyProvisions: The annual bonus is paid under a written plan approved by the Compensation Committee that states eligibility, target bonus by level, performance measures, funding formula, individual modifiers and payment timing.
Company funding is based on financial measures set at the start of the year (e.g., revenue and non-GAAP operating margin) with a 0-200% funding range; no demographic-linked metrics are used.

Individual award = target bonus x company funding x individual modifier (0-150%), with a compliance gate: an employee found to have committed a serious Code, export-control or anti-bribery violation receives no award.
Employees hired on or before [October 1] participate pro rata; periods of protected leave are prorated only as local law permits.
Awards are paid no later than March 15 following the plan year and, except where local law requires payment of earned amounts, require active employment on the payment date.
Finance reviews accruals quarterly, and Total Rewards and Finance review and approve payout calculations before they go to Payroll (SOX key control).
Spot and recognition awards above [USD 1,000] need VP approval; retention bonuses need Total Rewards and CHRO approval and are recorded with vesting schedules.
Discretionary adjustments to formula results for executive officers are made only by the Compensation Committee and disclosed as required.
All incentive compensation is subject to the Compensation Recovery policy.
Bonuses are included in overtime regular-rate calculations, vacation pay and statutory severance bases where local law requires.
policies.sampleLanguage:
Plan Purpose. The [Company] Annual Incentive Plan rewards employees for the Company's financial results and their individual contributions during the fiscal year.

Eligibility. Regular employees who do not participate in a sales incentive plan and who begin employment on or before October 1 are eligible. Awards for employees who join during the year, change eligibility or take an unpaid leave will be prorated, except where local law requires otherwise.

Funding and Awards. At the start of each fiscal year, the Compensation Committee approves the performance measures and goals used to determine the bonus pool, which may range from 0% to 200% of target. Individual awards are based on the bonus pool, the employee's target bonus and the employee's individual performance. An employee who has committed a serious violation of the Code of Business Conduct, export control laws or anti-corruption laws will not receive an award.

Payment. Awards are paid in the first quarter after the end of the fiscal year and no later than March 15. Except where local law provides otherwise, you must be employed on the payment date to receive an award.

Recovery. Awards are subject to the Company's Compensation Recovery Policy.

roles.duties: Approves plan design, goals, funding and executive awards.
Administers the plan, issues guidelines and calculates individual awards.
Sets and certifies financial results, accrues quarterly and validates total payouts.
Assess individual performance and recommend modifiers within guidelines.
Pays awards with correct tax treatment and regular-rate adjustments.

countryAddenda.us: Non-discretionary bonuses must be included in the FLSA regular rate for non-exempt employees, and bonuses are supplemental wages (22% withholding, 37% above $1M). Paying by March 15 keeps awards within the Section 409A short-term deferral rule.
countryAddenda.us-ca: Earned bonuses are wages that must be paid at separation, so the plan must state clearly that the award is not earned until the payment date; non-discretionary bonuses also enter the regular rate for overtime and meal and rest premiums. SB 642 counts bonuses as wages for Equal Pay Act purposes.
countryAddenda.ca: Bonuses integral to compensation are part of common-law reasonable notice damages unless the plan clearly and unambiguously removes them for the notice period (Matthews v. Ocean Nutrition, 2020 SCC 26), and vacation pay (4%/6%) applies to non-discretionary bonuses.
countryAddenda.in: Pay statutory bonus of 8.33%-20% to employees with wages up to INR 21,000 a month (calculated on the higher of INR 7,000 or minimum wage) within 8 months of year end (by 30 Nov); performance pay that pushes excluded items above 50% of remuneration counts as 'wages' under the Code on Wages. Recover joining or retention bonuses only as reasonable, pro-rated liquidated damages.
countryAddenda.tw: LSA Art. 29 requires a bonus or profit share for fault-free employees when there is net profit, and the Taiwan entity's articles must set an employee-compensation percentage (Company Act Art. 235-1). Regular performance bonuses may count as 'wages' for severance and pension purposes (verify), and the 2.11% NHI supplementary premium applies to bonuses above 4x the monthly insured salary in a year.
countryAddenda.cn: Bonuses are included in the 12-month average wage used for economic compensation (LCL Art. 47), and changes to bonus rules require democratic procedure or consent. The annual one-off bonus may be taxed separately once a year through 31 Dec 2027; employment-on-payment-date conditions hold only if clearly set out in the plan and handbook (verify local court practice).

decisions: Funding metrics: revenue and operating margin only, or also product milestones such as tape-outs? (Milestones must be objective to avoid disputes.)
Individual modifier range and whether to use a forced distribution? (Wider ranges differentiate more but draw pay-equity scrutiny.)
Employment-on-payment-date requirement by country? (Enforceable in most US states and in China with clear rules; limited in Canada and California.)
Annual or semiannual payout? (Semiannual payouts aid retention in India and Taiwan.)
ESG or diversity metrics in funding? (Avoid demographic-linked metrics given US DEI enforcement.)
pitfalls: Ambiguous plan language that makes bonuses 'earned' before payment, creating California final-pay and waiting-time exposure.
Cutting Canadian bonuses during the notice period without Matthews-compliant language.
Leaving bonuses out of the regular rate for non-exempt lab technicians.
Undocumented discretionary executive adjustments that then cannot be explained in the proxy.
policies.training: Manager briefing before each award cycle; participants acknowledge the plan document annually.

policies.name: Sales Compensation Governance
policies.owner: Sales Operations (plan administration) with Total Rewards (design) and Finance
policies.approver: Sales Compensation Committee (CRO, CFO, CHRO, General Counsel); Compensation Committee for executive sales leaders
policies.review: Annual, before each plan year; interim review for any material mid-year change
policies.audience: Employees on sales incentive plans: account managers, sales leaders, field application engineers (FAEs), channel and distribution managers
policies.purpose: Governs the design, documentation, crediting, calculation, payment and controls of sales incentive plans so they reward profitable, compliant design wins and revenue. It builds in legal requirements for written commission agreements, SOX and ASC 340-40 controls, and export-control and anti-bribery gates that regulators now expect in semiconductor sales pay.
keyProvisions: Each participant receives a written plan document and individual target letter before, or within 30 days of, the plan period start and signs an acknowledgment; the plan states how commissions are earned, calculated, credited and paid, including after termination.
Plan measures (bookings, revenue, design wins, gross margin) and quotas are approved by the Sales Compensation Committee, and quotas are set by documented methodology within 45 days of plan start.

No credit, commission or bonus is paid on orders that have not cleared restricted-party screening and export licensing, that ship in breach of export, sanctions or anti-bribery rules, or that involve undisclosed distributor discounts or side agreements; amounts paid on such orders are forfeited and recovered.
Crediting rules (territories, split credit, channel and distributor sales, design-win to revenue linkage) are documented, and disputes are decided by the Sales Compensation Committee within 30 days.
Windfall deals (a single transaction producing more than [2x] target incentive) are reviewed under criteria stated in the plan.
Draws and guarantees are documented with duration and recoverability, and recoverable draws are recovered only as local law permits.

Sales Operations and Finance review and approve commission calculations each period before payroll (SOX key control); segregation of duties prevents sales staff from both booking orders and clearing screening, or from calculating their own pay.
Commission costs are capitalized and amortized under ASC 340-40 by Finance.
Mid-year plan changes are prospective only, communicated in writing at least 30 days before they take effect where practicable, and meet local consent requirements.
On termination, earned commissions are paid under the plan and local final-pay rules.
All participants certify anti-bribery and export compliance annually, and China and APAC sales leaders carry a compliance modifier in their incentive.
policies.sampleLanguage:
Plan Documents. Your participation in the [Company] Sales Incentive Plan is governed by this Plan document and your individual Target Letter, which together describe your quota, measures, rates and payment timing. You must sign an acknowledgment of the Plan within 30 days of receiving it.

Earning Commissions. A commission is earned only when all conditions in the Plan are met, including shipment and recognition of revenue, receipt of any required export license and successful completion of restricted-party screening. No commission is earned on any transaction that violates export control, sanctions or anti-corruption laws or Company policy, or that involves an undisclosed side agreement. [Company] will recover any amounts paid on such transactions to the extent permitted by law.

Crediting and Disputes. Credit is assigned under the crediting rules in the Plan. Submit any dispute in writing to Sales Operations within 60 days of the statement date.

Changes. [Company] may amend the Plan prospectively with written notice. Changes will not reduce commissions already earned.

Termination. If your employment ends, commissions earned under the Plan will be paid in accordance with the Plan and applicable law.

roles.duties: Approves plan design, quotas, windfall reviews, exceptions and disputes.
Administers crediting and calculations, issues statements and keeps signed acknowledgments.
Reviews calculations, accrues commissions, manages ASC 340-40 capitalization and SOX evidence.
Confirm screening and licensing before credit and flag violating transactions for forfeiture.
Explain plans, validate credit and enforce compliant selling.
Pays commissions on time and applies local final-pay rules.

countryAddenda.us: Some states require signed written commission plans (e.g., NY Labor Law 191(1)(c); MN) and regulate post-termination payment, and unclear plans risk treble damages under state wage laws. Include commissions in the regular rate for any non-exempt sales staff and confirm outside-sales exemption status.
countryAddenda.us-ca: Labor Code 2751 requires a written commission contract stating how commissions are computed and paid, with a signed receipt from the employee; earned commissions are due immediately on discharge (or under LC 202 on resignation). Recover draws or advances only by agreement and never through deductions that breach LC 221 or 224; commissions are wages for Equal Pay Act purposes (SB 642).
countryAddenda.ca: Vacation pay (4%/6%) applies to commissions, and commissions forming part of regular pay are included in common-law notice damages unless clearly excluded (Matthews). Mid-year reductions to plans can be constructive dismissal without consent or reasonable notice.
countryAddenda.in: Commissions are excluded from 'wages' only up to the 50% limit; where excluded items exceed 50% of remuneration the excess counts toward PF, gratuity and retrenchment (Code on Wages s.2(y)). Keep anti-bribery certifications as part of the 'adequate procedures' defense under Prevention of Corruption Act s.9.
countryAddenda.tw: Regularly paid commissions are likely 'wages' for severance, pension-contribution and overtime calculations (verify), and plan changes that reduce pay need consent. Put commission rules in the contract and itemize commissions on pay statements, withholding NHI supplementary premium on large payouts.
countryAddenda.cn: Commissions form part of wages for the 12-month average used for economic compensation, and plan changes need democratic procedure or consent (LCL Arts. 4, 35); check Shanghai's 2026 wage-payment measures for the overtime base (verify treatment of commissions). Build commercial-bribery (AUCL) and export-control gates into credit rules for distributor and SOE customer sales.

decisions: Pay on bookings, shipments or revenue recognition? (Revenue-linked pay reduces clawbacks but delays payment; design wins may merit a separate milestone bonus.)
Uncapped commissions or caps with windfall review? (Uncapped plans motivate; windfall clauses need clear criteria to be enforceable.)
FAE incentives: team-based bonus or individual commission? (Team bonuses reduce pressure to overpromise or bypass export gates.)
Weight of the compliance modifier for China and APAC leaders? (DOJ and BIS credit compliance-linked pay.)
Recoverable or non-recoverable draws for new representatives?
pitfalls: Unsigned or late plan documents in California, leading to disputes and penalties.
Paying commissions on orders later found to be unlicensed shipments to restricted parties (Cadence, 2025).
Sales staff able to override screening holds or influence their own crediting.
Mid-year quota increases without notice or consent, creating wage and constructive-dismissal claims.
policies.training: Plan training and signed acknowledgment at each plan start; annual export-control and anti-bribery certification for all participants.

policies.name: Equity Grant Policy
policies.owner: Total Rewards (design) with Stock Admin (administration) and Legal (Securities)
policies.approver: Compensation Committee (grant authority, delegations, grant calendar); Board and shareholders for plan adoption and share reserve
policies.review: Annual; with each share-reserve proposal or plan amendment
policies.audience: All equity recipients (employees, new hires, executives, directors and eligible consultants) and everyone who recommends, approves or administers grants
policies.purpose: Sets how equity awards (RSUs, PSUs, options, ESPP) are authorized, sized, timed, priced, documented and administered so that grants comply with the plan, Nasdaq listing rules, SEC disclosure rules (including Item 402(x) on option timing), tax rules and local securities and exchange-control laws. Equity is central to pay for semiconductor engineers, so consistent governance also protects retention value and pay equity.
keyProvisions: All grants are made under a shareholder-approved plan (Nasdaq 5635(c)); inducement grants to new hires outside the plan require approval by independent directors or the Compensation Committee and a press release announcing material terms.

The Compensation Committee approves all grants to directors and Section 16 officers (non-employee director approval supports the Rule 16b-3 exemption) and delegates non-executive grants to an equity award committee within written limits on share numbers, award types and per-person caps.

Grants are made only on pre-set dates: new-hire and promotion grants on the [15th] of the month after the start or effective date (or the next trading day), annual refresh grants on one fixed date; grants are never timed to take advantage of MNPI.

Stock options are not granted to executive officers from four business days before to one business day after filing a 10-Q, 10-K or MNPI-disclosing 8-K (Item 402(x)), and option exercise prices are at least the closing price on the grant date.
RSU grant values convert to shares using a trailing [30]-trading-day average price under grant guidelines by level and location approved annually.
Standard vesting: new-hire RSUs over 4 years (25% after 1 year, then quarterly); refresh RSUs quarterly over 3-4 years; PSUs vest only on performance certified by the Committee.
Offer letters state only a target grant value subject to approval, never a share count; award agreements with country appendices must be accepted within 90 days.
Repricing underwater options requires shareholder approval unless the plan expressly permits it.
Treatment on termination, leave, death, disability and change in control follows the plan and award agreement; any acceleration outside those terms requires Compensation Committee approval.
Stock Admin reconciles the equity platform to the cap table and ASC 718 expense quarterly, with segregation of duties between grant entry and approval.
Burn rate and overhang are modeled annually against the share reserve and proxy-advisor guidelines.
All awards are subject to the Insider Trading and Compensation Recovery policies.
policies.sampleLanguage:
Authority. All equity awards must be approved by the Compensation Committee of the Board or by an officer or committee acting under a written delegation from the Committee, and must be granted under a shareholder-approved equity plan or, for new hires, as a properly approved inducement award. No manager or recruiter may promise a specific number of shares; offer letters may state only a target grant value, subject to approval.

Grant Dates. Awards are granted only on the dates set in the Company's grant calendar. New-hire and promotion awards are granted on the 15th day of the month after the employee's start or promotion date. Annual awards are granted on a single date each year. [Company] does not time the grant of equity awards to take advantage of material nonpublic information.

Calculation. The number of restricted stock units in an award is determined by dividing the approved grant value by the average closing price of [Company] stock over the 30 trading days before the grant date.

Terms. Each award is subject to the terms of the plan and the award agreement, including any country-specific appendix, the Insider Trading Policy and the Compensation Recovery Policy.

roles.duties: Approves grant guidelines, executive and director grants, delegations, the grant calendar and inducement grants.
Designs guidelines, models burn rate and overhang and prepares grant recommendations.
Enters approved grants, manages acceptance and vesting, reconciles records and enforces blackout blocks.
Reviews plan compliance, Item 402(x), 8-K and Form 4 obligations and country securities filings.
Withholds and reports tax at vesting or exercise in each country and sources income for mobile employees.

countryAddenda.us: Options must be priced at or above grant-date fair market value to stay outside Section 409A; ISO treatment is limited to $100,000 first exercisable per year, and a Section 423 ESPP is capped at $25,000 per calendar year, with Forms 3921/3922 due by Jan 31. RSU vesting is supplemental wages (22%, or 37% above $1M), and from 2027 Section 162(m) adds the five highest-paid other employees.
countryAddenda.us-ca: SB 642 treats stock and options as wages for Equal Pay Act purposes, so include equity in pay-equity audits, and confirm the California securities exemption for plan grants (Corporations Code 25102(o); verify). Avoid any repayment of vested equity on departure that could be framed as a stay-or-pay term under AB 692.
countryAddenda.ca: Draft forfeiture language to exclude the common-law notice period expressly and unambiguously (Matthews v. Ocean Nutrition, 2020 SCC 26), or RSUs vesting during notice become damages; settle RSUs within 3 years to avoid salary-deferral-arrangement rules (verify). The stock option deduction is capped at C$200,000 of annual vesting value for large non-CCPC employers, and ESPP discounts are taxable.
countryAddenda.in: RSU and option perquisites are taxed as salary at vesting or exercise, with Indian payroll TDS under the Income-tax Act 2025, and employees must report foreign shares in Schedule FA; ESPP purchases by residents fall under FEMA ODI/LRS rules. Recharge arrangements with the parent affect corporate deductibility and transfer pricing.
countryAddenda.tw: Confirm the tax treatment and employer reporting of RSU and option income for Taiwan employees and any securities or foreign-exchange filings for offering parent shares (verify), and benchmark equity against local employee-compensation profit-sharing. Provide a Traditional Chinese summary of award terms.
countryAddenda.cn: Register the plan with SAFE under Circular 7 through the WFOE before employees participate, keep the special FX account for proceeds and update registrations for material changes; withhold IIT at vesting or exercise, using separate taxation of listed-company equity income through 31 Dec 2027. State termination forfeiture clearly in the award agreement and the handbook.

decisions: Grant guidelines by value or by fixed share numbers? (Value-based with a trailing average price is standard.)
Monthly or quarterly new-hire grant dates? (Monthly improves offer competitiveness; quarterly simplifies administration.)
Refresh vesting: 1-year cliff or quarterly from the start? (No cliff on refreshes is common in semiconductors.)
Delegation limits for the equity award committee (e.g., value per grant, no Section 16 officers)?
Eligibility: broad-based to all engineers or limited to certain levels? (Broad eligibility helps retention but raises burn rate.)
Use PSUs for vice presidents below executive-officer level?
pitfalls: Recruiters promising share counts instead of grant values in offers.
Granting options to officers inside Item 402(x) windows without planning for the disclosure.
Canadian award agreements that forfeit on 'termination date' without addressing the notice period.
China employees participating before SAFE registration, blocking FX repatriation.
Delegated grants that exceed written delegation limits and may be invalid.
policies.training: Equity education for new grantees at their first grant; annual training for Stock Admin and Total Rewards on plan terms and Item 402(x); annual Compensation Committee briefing.
