policies.name: Payroll & Wage Payment
policies.owner: Global Payroll with People Ops
policies.approver: CFO + CHRO; Controller for SOX controls
policies.review: Annual + on law or rate change (minimum wages, social insurance bases, tax forms)
policies.audience: All employees on Company payroll in every entity; managers approving time and pay changes; HR, Payroll, Finance and payroll vendors
policies.purpose: Makes sure employees are paid accurately and on time in line with each country's wage-payment, deduction, tax and social insurance rules, under SOX internal controls. It sets pay frequency, final-pay timing, lawful deductions, error correction and access controls for an equity-heavy, multi-country payroll.
keyProvisions: Each entity pays on a published pay calendar that meets the legal minimum frequency: US semi-monthly or bi-weekly (per state), Canada bi-weekly or semi-monthly, India monthly before the 7th of the following month, Taiwan monthly, China monthly on a fixed date.

Every employee receives an itemized pay statement for each pay date with all legally required content (hours and rates for non-exempt staff, deductions, leave balances where required, employer legal name).
Only approved Darwinbox transactions (hire, pay change, leave, termination) and approved timekeeping data can change payroll; email or verbal instructions are never accepted.

Deductions are limited to statutory deductions, voluntary deductions authorized in writing and others permitted by local law; the Company never deducts for equipment loss, training costs or penalties except where local law expressly permits.
Payroll changes close [5] business days before pay date; off-cycle payments are limited to final pay, required corrections and approved exceptions.
HR notifies Payroll of every separation as soon as it is decided, and final pay (earned wages, legally payable leave, earned commissions and statutory amounts) is paid within the local deadline.

Underpayments are corrected by off-cycle payment within [3] business days of confirmation, or sooner where law requires; overpayments are recovered only with written employee agreement or as local law permits, and never below minimum wage.
Equity income (RSU vesting, option exercises, ESPP discounts) is reported and withheld in each taxing jurisdiction, including multi-jurisdiction sourcing for mobile employees.

Payroll variance reports are reviewed and approved by someone independent of data entry before each payroll is released, and quarterly access reviews confirm no single user can create a worker, change pay and approve payroll.
Payroll vendors provide SOC 1 Type II reports annually, and complementary user-entity controls are operated and evidenced.
Payroll records are retained under the Records Retention schedule (e.g., US 3-4 years, Canada 6 years, Taiwan 5 years, China at least 2 years for wage records).
policies.sampleLanguage:
Paying You Correctly and On Time. [Company] pays employees on the regular paydays published for each country. You will receive a pay statement for each pay period that shows your earnings, hours where applicable, deductions and other information required by local law. Please review your pay statement and report any error to Payroll at [contact] as soon as possible.

Changes to Pay. Changes to your pay or payroll information take effect only after they are approved in our HR system. Managers and HR must never instruct Payroll to change an employee's pay by email or conversation.

Deductions. [Company] makes only deductions that are required by law, that you have authorized in writing, or that are otherwise permitted by local law. We do not deduct fines or penalties from wages.

Corrections. If you have been underpaid, we will correct the error promptly and no later than the time required by law. If you have been overpaid, Payroll will contact you to agree on a repayment plan that complies with local law and will not reduce your pay below the legal minimum.

Final Pay. When your employment ends, you will receive your final pay by the deadline required in your location.

roles.duties: Runs payroll cycles, statutory filings, variance review and error correction, and manages vendors.
Enters accurate, timely HRIS transactions, including separation dates the day they are decided.
Approve time and pay changes before cut-off and report errors promptly.
The Controller owns SOX controls over payroll, accruals and reconciliations.
Processes payroll under contract, files statutory returns and provides SOC 1 reports.
Keep personal, bank and tax information current and review pay statements.

countryAddenda.us: Follow each work state's pay-frequency, final-pay and deduction rules (many require written authorization and restrict self-help overpayment recovery, e.g., NY Labor Law 193, Illinois), and register for withholding, UI and PFML in each remote employee's state before the first payroll. Report qualified overtime (code TT) on 2026 Forms W-2, apply supplemental withholding (22%, or 37% above $1M) to RSU income, and use the 2026 Social Security wage base of $184,500.
countryAddenda.us-ca: Non-exempt staff are paid at least semi-monthly within 7 days after the pay period closes, with itemized statements meeting LC 226 (including the paid sick leave balance; penalties up to $4,000 per employee plus PAGA). Final pay including accrued vacation is due immediately on discharge, within 72 hours of a resignation without notice or on the last day with 72+ hours' notice, with waiting-time penalties up to 30 days' wages (LC 201-203), and no deductions for equipment loss except for dishonesty, willful act or gross negligence (LC 221, 224).
countryAddenda.ca: Ontario: a regular recurring payday with itemized statements, direct deposit to an account the employee chooses, and final pay by the later of 7 days after termination or the next regular payday; BC: at least semi-monthly within 8 days after the pay period, and final pay within 48 hours of employer termination or 6 days after a quit. Deductions need written authorization and statutory permission; 2026 rates are CPP 5.95% to C$74,600, CPP2 4% to C$85,000 and EI 1.63% to C$68,900, with T4s filed by the end of February.
countryAddenda.in: Monthly wages are due before the 7th of the following month and final dues within 2 working days of separation, including resignation (Code on Wages s.17), with deductions limited to authorized items within 50% of wages (s.18). Apply the 50% 'wages' rule to PF and gratuity bases and the INR 25,000 EPF ceiling (from 17 Sep 2026), withhold TDS under Income-tax Act 2025 s.392 with quarterly Form 138 and Form 130 issued by 15 June, and remit professional tax.
countryAddenda.tw: Pay in NTD, in full and directly, at least monthly by agreement, with an itemized statement (LSA Arts. 22-23), and never pre-deduct damages or penalties (Art. 26); settle wages immediately at termination, including unused annual leave, and pay severance within 30 days. Minimum wage is NT$29,500 a month or NT$196 an hour (2026); withhold Labor Insurance, NHI and the 2.11% supplementary premium, and keep wage records 5 years.
countryAddenda.cn: Pay at least monthly in RMB on a fixed date with itemized statements; deductions for employee-caused losses are capped at 20% of monthly wage and cannot reduce pay below minimum wage (Shanghai RMB 2,740; Shenzhen RMB 2,700 from 1 Sept 2026). Contribute social insurance and housing fund on the actual wage base within city limits (Shanghai RMB 7,546-37,731 from 1 Jul 2026), withhold IIT monthly by the 15th, pay final wages in full at termination and keep wage records at least 2 years.

decisions: One global payroll aggregator or separate in-country providers? (An aggregator improves controls and reporting; in-country specialists handle China and India complexity.)
US pay frequency: bi-weekly or semi-monthly? (Semi-monthly suits exempt salaries and California rules; bi-weekly suits hourly calculations.)
Payroll ownership: Finance or HR? (SOX favors Finance ownership with HR-owned input controls.)
Overpayment recovery: always seek repayment, or write off below a threshold (e.g., USD 100)?
Allow pay cards, or direct deposit only? (Several jurisdictions require payment to an account the employee chooses.)
pitfalls: Late termination entries causing overpayments, erroneous RSU vesting and California waiting-time penalties.
Running a 30-60 day India full-and-final cycle instead of 2 working days.
Deducting unreturned laptops from final pay in California, Taiwan or China.
Not registering a remote employee's new state before the first payroll.
Payroll administrators with rights both to change pay and to approve payroll.
policies.training: Quarterly country-update training for the Payroll team; manager guidance on time approval and pay-change cut-offs at manager onboarding; HRBPs acknowledge pay-change approval rules annually.
